get.summary: Get all enabled feature flags for the current user.
Get who you are: your user account and the employee it is linked to.
get.description: Call this first whenever a request is about the person asking ("my", "me", "I"): never list users or employees to find yourself, which needs permissions most people do not hold. Wayd records people as employees, so `employee.id` is the UUID that employeeId, role and assignee parameters take for you, and `userId` is only for parameters that say they take a user id. `employee` is null when your account is not linked to an employee. For your teams, allocations and work items use Me_GetTeamMemberships, Me_GetAllocations and Me_GetWorkItems; for projects where you hold a role, Projects_GetProjects with `role` and no `employeeId`.

get.summary: List the teams and teams of teams you are a member of.
get.description: Returns one entry per team or team of teams your employee belongs to, sorted by team name, each with the member roles you hold on it. Needs no View Employees permission. Membership is not allocation: Me_GetAllocations says how much of your time each team has. Returns 404 when your account is not linked to an employee.

get.summary: Get how your time is allocated to teams over time.
get.description: Returns every allocation of your employee across all teams in date order: the team, the role the time is spent in when one was chosen, the date range (`end` is null when it has no end) and the `percent` of your time. Needs no View Employees permission. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or your account is not linked to an employee.

get.summary: Get the work items assigned to you.
get.description: Your tickets: the backlog-level (Requirement tier) work items assigned to your employee across every workspace; epics, features and tasks are left out. `statusCategories` narrows them to any of the codes `Proposed`, `Active`, `Done` and `Removed` — pass `Proposed` and `Active` for open work. `doneFrom` and `doneTo` keep only work items finished in that window, so either one leaves out work not yet done; a time without a zone is read as UTC. Needs the Work Items view permission. Returns 404 when your account is not linked to an employee.

get.summary: List the records you follow.
get.description: Returns one page of the records you follow — projects, programs, planning interval objectives and intake requests together — with each record's `ownerType`, `id`, `key`, `name`, `statusName`, `lifecycle` (`NotStarted`, `Active`, `Completed`, `Canceled`), `health` (`Healthy`, `AtRisk`, `Unhealthy`, or null when it has none), when you followed it and when it `lastChangedOn`; an objective also carries `parentKey` and `parentName`, its planning interval, and an intake request its desk. A record you can no longer read is left out of the page and the total. Narrow with `ownerType` (`ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; any other value returns 400), `view` (`Unhealthy`, `ChangedRecently` for the last seven days, `Closed` for records that have finished, whatever the outcome: completed, canceled, or a missed objective) and `search` (matched against the name, or the key exactly). `sort` is `LastChanged` (default) or `Followed`, and `direction` is `Descending` (default, most recent first) or `Ascending`; a record with no activity counts as the least recently changed, so it comes last when descending and first when ascending. `page` starts at 1; `pageSize` is at most 500. Following a record tells you about its changes through your notifications. Requires the following feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Count the records you follow, by kind and by what needs a look.
get.description: Returns the `total` you follow and can still read, a count per kind of record you can read (`types`, each with `ownerType`, `displayName` and `count`, including kinds you follow none of), and a count per view (`views`: `Unhealthy`, `ChangedRecently`, `Closed`). Records you can no longer read are not counted. Requires the following feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get a record you follow, with what has happened since you followed it.
get.description: Returns the record as `Me_GetFollows` lists it (`record`), plus `progress` (0–100, objectives only), `people` (each with a `role`, a `name` and the `employeeId` of a person, null for a team: a project's or program's owners then managers, an objective's team, an intake request's assignee then requester), `start` and `end` (an intake request's `end` is its need-by date), and `changesSinceFollowed`: its activity since you followed it, newest first, at most 20 — `hasMoreChanges` says whether there is more. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Returns 404 when you do not follow the record or can no longer read it, and 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires the following feature flag.

get.summary: Get whether you follow a record.
get.description: Returns `isFollowing` and, when true, `followedOn`. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Returns 404 when the record does not exist or you cannot read it — even if you followed it before losing access — and 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires the following feature flag.

put.summary: Follow a record.
put.description: Follows the record for you. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Following a record you already follow changes nothing and still succeeds. You can follow only what you can read: returns 404 when the record does not exist or you cannot read it, and 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Following grants no access; it tells you about the record's changes through your notifications. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

delete.summary: Stop following a record.
delete.description: Removes your follow of the record. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Succeeds whether or not you followed it, and works on a record you can no longer read. Returns 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

get.summary: List the records you have muted.
get.description: Returns one page of the records you have muted, most recently muted first: each with `ownerType`, `id`, `key`, `name`, `statusName`, `lifecycle`, `isFollowing` (muting never stops following) and `mutedOn`; an objective also carries `parentKey` and `parentName`, its planning interval, and an intake request its desk. A muted record tells you nothing more, whatever the reason. A record you can no longer read is left out of the page and the total. `page` starts at 1; `pageSize` is at most 500. Requires the following feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get whether you have muted a record.
get.description: Returns `isMuted` and, when true, `mutedOn`. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Returns 404 when the record does not exist or you cannot read it, and 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires the following feature flag.

put.summary: Mute a record.
put.description: Mutes the record for you: you are told nothing more about it, whether you follow it, take part in it, or both, and your unread notifications about it are marked read. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Muting a record you already muted changes nothing and still succeeds; `wasAlreadyMuted` says which happened, so an undo unmutes only a mute this call made. Muting changes nothing else: you keep your access and your roles, and you still follow the record if you did. Unmuting brings back nothing that happened while it was muted. You can mute only what you can read: returns 404 when the record does not exist or you cannot read it, and 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

delete.summary: Unmute a record.
delete.description: Removes your mute of the record, so its later changes notify you again. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Succeeds whether or not you had muted it, and works on a record you can no longer read. Returns 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

get.summary: List the reasons you can mute, and which you have.
get.description: Returns one entry per reason you can be told for: `reason` (`Following`: records you follow; `Participant`: records you hold a role on, or whose team you belong to), `isMuted`, and `mutedOn` when muted. A muted reason stops only that reason, on every record: if you follow a project and also take part in it, muting `Participant` still tells you about it because you follow it. Requires the following feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

put.summary: Mute a reason.
put.description: Stops telling you about any record for `reason` (`Following` or `Participant`); you are still told for any other reason that applies. Muting a reason you already muted changes nothing and still succeeds. Muting changes no follow, role or access, and leaves the notifications you already have. Returns 422 for any other reason. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

delete.summary: Unmute a reason.
delete.description: Removes your mute of `reason`, so later changes tell you for it again. Succeeds whether or not you had muted it. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

get.summary: List your notifications.
get.description: Returns one page of your notifications, one entry per record, newest change first. Each entry has the `record` (`ownerType`, `id`, `key`, `name`, `statusName`; an objective also carries `parentKey` and `parentName`, its planning interval, and an intake request its desk), the newest change — `event` (`Created`, `StatusChanged`, `LifecycleChanged`, `HealthReported`, `TimelineChanged`, `RolesChanged`, `Reparented`, `ScoreRecorded`), `eventId`, `occurredOn`, `actorKind` and `actor` (null when no employee is linked to whoever made it) — the `reasons` you were told (`Following`, `Participant`, and later `Requester`, `Assigned`, `Mentioned`), `unreadCount`, `count`, `isUnread` and `latestNotificationId`. You are never told about your own changes, or about imports. A record you can no longer read is left out. `unreadOnly` keeps only entries with something unread. `pageSize` is at most 500. For the next page, pass the response's `nextCursor` as `before`; `nextCursor` is null on the last page. Paging by cursor means an entry that moves to the top while you read on is neither repeated nor skipped; it appears when you read the first page again. Requires the following feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Count the records you have unread notifications about.
get.description: Returns `count`, the number of records with unread notifications you can still read, and `isCapped`, true when there are more than 99 — `count` is then 99, shown as "99+". Requires the following feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

post.summary: Mark one notification read.
post.description: Marks the notification with this `id` — an entry's `latestNotificationId` — read. Marking one already read changes nothing. Returns 404 when you have no notification with that id. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

post.summary: Mark your notifications about one record read.
post.description: Marks every notification you have about the record read — the whole entry the list shows for it. `ownerType` is `ppm.project`, `ppm.program`, `planning.planning-interval-objective` or `demand.intake-request`; `ownerId` is the record's UUID, not its key. Succeeds whether or not anything was unread. Returns 400 for an owner type that cannot be followed. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

post.summary: Mark all your notifications read.
post.description: Marks every notification you have read. Succeeds whether or not anything was unread. Requires your account to be linked to an employee (403 otherwise) and the following feature flag.

get.summary: Global search across all modules.
Get the IANA time zones that can be chosen.
Get a list of sprints.
get.description: Every sprint of every team, or of one team when `teamId` (the team's UUID) is given; pass it whenever the team is known, since the full list is long. Each sprint has a UUID `id` and an integer `key`, its planned `start` and `end`, its `state` now (Future, Active or Completed, worked out from its actual and planned dates), the `started` and `completed` moments the team recorded, and its `sprintType`.

get.summary: Get a list of all sprint types.
get.description: The sprint types and what each means: Standard, comparable with the team's other sprints, and NonStandard, left out of the team's sprint metrics. Each `code` is the value `Sprints_SetSprintType` takes.

get.summary: Get sprint details.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. Besides its dates, state, team and type, it says what the caller can do now: `canManageSprint` (the caller may start, complete or reopen it), `canStart`, `canComplete` and `canReopen` (the sprint's lifecycle allows it, whoever asks), `startWindow` and `completeWindow` (the moments a start or completion may be recorded at), and `openSprint`, another of the team's sprints still open that starting this one would complete. Read it before any sprint lifecycle call.

get.summary: Get activity history for the sprint.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. Newest first: syncs changing its details, dates or team, and the team starting, completing or reopening it, correcting its actual dates, setting its team days off or its type. Each entry has a `category`, an `actorKind` with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string, carrying the value before and after a change. Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

get.summary: Get sprint backlog items.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. The work items in the sprint now, in backlog rank order. For what the sprint committed to and what became of it, use `Sprints_GetScope`.

get.summary: Get sprint work item metrics.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. Counts and estimates of the work in the sprint now — total, completed, in progress, not started and unestimated — with a cycle-time rollup. Estimates are in `sizingMethod`, the team's on the sprint's planned start. Not history: for the commitment and what became of it use `Sprints_GetScope`, and for the trend `Sprints_GetBurn`.

get.summary: Get sprint scope.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. What the sprint committed to and what became of it, worked out from work item history between its effective start and end: each requirement-tier item that was in the sprint, whether it was committed or added, and whether it was completed, completed as Removed, carried over or descoped. Not found when the sprint has no planned dates.

get.summary: Get sprint burn-up and burn-down.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. The sprint's requirement-tier scope and completed work at its commitment point, at the end of each of its days in the team's zone, and at its effective end — or now, for a sprint that has not ended — as counts and estimates, worked out from work item history. Agrees with the sprint scope report at the commitment point and the end. Not found when the sprint has no planned dates.

get.summary: Get a sprint's capacity beside its scope.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the sprint's UUID `id` or integer `key`. The team's capacity over the sprint's planned dates (`start` to `end`) in person-days after holidays and time away: `allocatedPersonDays` in every role, `deliveryPersonDays` in roles that count toward delivery capacity, and `awayPersonDays` that time away took. Beside it, the sprint's `scope` in `sizingMethod` (by count under Count): the work in the sprint now before its commitment point (`scopeBasis` Planned), and the committed work after it (Committed). `expectedScope` is what the capacity is expected to deliver: the team's velocity per person-day of delivery capacity over the completed sprints its sprint metrics count now that ended no later than this sprint (`priorSprints`), in the same unit, times this sprint's. A sprint some way back therefore draws on fewer prior sprints than the team had at the time, or none. `isOverCapacity` is true when the scope is above it on a sprint that has not ended. `outcome` says whether the comparison was made, or why not: NoCapacity, NoPriorSprints, NoPriorCapacity. Not found when the sprint has no team or no planned dates. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

post.summary: Start a sprint.
post.description: Records that the team started the sprint, now or at an earlier startedAt inside its start window. `id` is the sprint's UUID; an integer key is not accepted. Requires membership of the sprint's team or its team of teams, and a caller linked to an employee. When another of the team's sprints is open, completeOpenSprintId must name it to confirm completing it at the same moment. `Sprints_GetSprint` reports `canStart`, the `startWindow` and the `openSprint`.

post.summary: Complete a sprint.
post.description: Records that the team completed the sprint, now or at an earlier completedAt inside its completion window. `id` is the sprint's UUID. Requires membership of the sprint's team or its team of teams, and a caller linked to an employee. `Sprints_GetSprint` reports `canComplete` and the `completeWindow`.

post.summary: Reopen a sprint.
post.description: Clears a completed sprint's completion while the team has not started a later sprint. `id` is the sprint's UUID. Requires membership of the sprint's team or its team of teams, and a caller linked to an employee. `Sprints_GetSprint` reports `canReopen`.

put.summary: Set a sprint's team days off.
put.description: Replaces the days within the sprint's planned dates that the whole team is off, such as an offsite, each with the `percentOff` of the working day (100, a full day, when left out). A day off takes its share of everyone's capacity that day, and the sprint's ideal burn-down drops that much less: flat on a full day off, half a day on a half day. `id` is the sprint's UUID. The list replaces the sprint's team days off: a day left out is removed and an empty list clears them, so read `teamDaysOff` from `Sprints_GetSprint` and send back the days that should stay. Requires membership of the sprint's team or its team of teams, and a caller linked to an employee.

put.summary: Set or clear a sprint's type.
put.description: Sets the type the team gives the sprint, held whatever its planning interval mapping says; a null type clears it, so the sprint follows the mapped iteration's category again. A non-standard sprint keeps its own metrics but is left out of the team's sprint metrics. `id` is the sprint's UUID; `sprintType` is Standard, NonStandard or null. Requires membership of the sprint's team or its team of teams, and a caller linked to an employee.

put.summary: Correct sprints' actual dates.
put.description: Replaces the actual start and completion of one or more of a team's sprints; an omitted value reverts to the sprint's default. Sprints corrected together are checked against each other's corrected dates, and the team's actual sprint periods may not overlap. Each entry takes a sprint's UUID `sprintId` and replaces both its `started` and `completed`, so send the current value of the one you are not changing (`started` and `completed` from `Sprints_GetSprint`), or it reverts to the planned date. Neither may be in the future. Requires membership of the sprints' team or its team of teams, and a caller linked to an employee.

get.summary: Get planning intervals that this sprint is mapped to.
get.description: `key` takes the sprint's integer `key` only, not its UUID. Returns each planning interval the sprint is mapped to through one of its iterations, by name; an unmapped sprint returns an empty list.

get.summary: Get a list of work processes.
get.description: A work process defines the work types a workspace's work items can have and the workflow each follows; work processes sync from an external system such as Azure DevOps (`ownership` Managed). Each has a UUID `id` and an integer `key`. Active work processes only unless `includeInactive` is true.

get.summary: Get work process details.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the work process's UUID `id` or integer `key`. For its work types and their workflows, use `WorkProcesses_GetSchemes`.

get.summary: Get activity history for the work process.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the work process's UUID `id` or integer `key`. Newest first; for a work process this is its integration state changing, as it is activated, deactivated or synced. Each entry has a `category`, an `actorKind` with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string. Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

post.summary: Activate a work process.
post.description: `id` is the work process's UUID. Only an active work process can be assigned to a workspace. Refused when it is already active.

post.summary: Deactivate a work process.
post.description: `id` is the work process's UUID. Refused while an active workspace uses it, and when it is already inactive.

get.summary: Get work process schemes.
get.description: `id` is the work process's UUID only. Returns one scheme per work type in the process: the `workType` (with its level), the `workflow` it follows, and whether the work type is active in this process. Returns 404 when no work process has the id.

get.summary: Get a list of workspaces.
get.description: Each workspace has a UUID `id`, a `key` (2 to 20 uppercase letters and digits, the prefix of its work item keys, such as `CORE` in `CORE-123`) and an `ownership`: Managed when it syncs from an external system such as Azure DevOps, Owned when Wayd holds it. Active workspaces only unless `includeInactive` is true.

get.summary: Get workspace details.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or its `key` (such as `CORE`). Returns its ownership, its work process, and the `externalViewWorkItemUrlTemplate` that links its work items to the source system.

put.summary: Set the external view work item URL template for a workspace.
put.description: Takes the workspace's UUID `id` only. The template is the URL prefix a work item's external id is appended to, giving each work item's `externalViewWorkItemUrl` (for Azure DevOps, something like `https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_workitems/edit/`), at most 256 characters, trimmed. Null, empty or whitespace clears it. Only a Managed workspace, one synced from an external system, takes a template.

get.summary: Get work items for a workspace.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or its `key`. Returns every work item in the workspace, in key order, which can be thousands: to find particular items, prefer `Workspaces_SearchWorkItems`, or a team's or project's work item tools.

get.summary: Get work item details.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or its `key`, the prefix of the work item key; `workItemKey` takes the work item key, such as `CORE-123`. A work item UUID is not accepted.

get.summary: Get a work item's project info.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or `key`; `workItemKey` the work item key. Returns the work item's own `project`, the `parentProject` it would otherwise inherit, and `projectSource`: WorkItem (its own assignment), Parent (inherited) or None. Read it before `Workspaces_UpdateWorkItemProject`.

put.summary: Update the project for a work item.
put.description: Sets a Portfolio-tier work item's own project; other tiers are refused. `id` is the workspace's UUID, and `workItemId` the work item's UUID, which must match `workItemId` in the body; a work item key is not accepted. Returns 404 when the work item is not in that workspace. A null `projectId` clears the item's own project so it inherits its parent's again, and choosing the parent's project is the same as inheriting it. Work items beneath it that have no project of their own inherit the change.

get.summary: Get a work item's child work items.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or `key`; `workItemKey` the parent's work item key. Returns its direct children only, in backlog rank order. Only Portfolio-tier work items have children.

get.summary: Get a work item's dependencies.
get.description: `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or `key`; `workItemKey` the work item key. Returns its current dependency links, oldest first, each naming the other work item (`dependency`) and its `type` from this item's side: Predecessor when this item waits on it, Successor when it waits on this item. `state`, `health` and `scope` describe the link.

get.summary: Forecast when a work item will be done, by Monte Carlo simulation of its team's recent throughput, its position in the team's backlog (everything ahead of it counts; active work comes first unless `startedWorkFirst` is false), and the open predecessors it waits on.
get.description: A portfolio work item (an Epic or Feature, say) is forecast from its open backlog descendants. Returns an `outcome` (Forecast, Done, Not Enough History, Blocked by Dependency, Cannot Forecast, Nothing Remaining), `backlogPosition`, and on Forecast completion `percentiles` (a `date` per `confidence`), plus `chanceOfFinishingByTargetDate` (0 to 1) when `targetDate` is given. `issues` explain what could not be forecast (No Team, Not a Backlog Item, Not Enough History); `dependencies` gives each predecessor's `shareOfTrialsSettingFinish`. Requires the delivery-forecasting feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get metrics for a work item.
get.description: A daily cumulative flow of the work item's Requirement-tier work, itself or, for a Portfolio-tier item, its descendants: for each `date` from the earliest creation to the day it was done (or today), how many items were Proposed, Active and Done. Removed work is left out. `idOrKey` takes the workspace's UUID `id` or `key`; `workItemKey` the work item key.

get.summary: Search for a work item using its key or title.
get.description: Searches every workspace: `query` matches part of a work item's key, its parent's key, or its title (a word prefix when full-text search is available). Returns at most `top` work items (default 50) in key order. Each result's `workspace` key and `key` are what the other work item tools take.

get.summary: Get a list of all work status categories.
get.description: The fixed categories every workflow places its statuses in, so work can be compared across workflows: Proposed (not started), Active (in progress), Done (completed) and Removed (left without being completed), in that order.

get.summary: Get a list of all work statuses.
get.description: The statuses work items can be in, such as New, In Progress or Done, by name, each with an integer `id`. A status has no category of its own: each workflow places it in a work status category. Active statuses only unless `includeInactive` is true.

post.summary: Create a work status.
post.description: Returns the new status's integer id. The name must be unique and can never be changed. Statuses are normally created by syncing a work process from the source system, which reuses an existing status of the same name.

get.summary: Get work status details using the id.

put.summary: Update a work status.
put.description: Changes a status's description, the only field that can change; its name cannot. `id` must match `id` in the body. A whole-record overwrite: an omitted description is cleared, so read the status first and pass back what should stay.

get.summary: Get a list of all work type levels.
get.description: The levels that order work types into a hierarchy, each with an integer `id`, its `tier` and its `order` within the tier, where 1 is the top level (Epics above Features, say): a Portfolio-tier parent must be at a higher level than a Portfolio-tier child. Listed by tier, and within a tier from the bottom level up. A work type's level sets its tier.

post.summary: Create a work type level.
post.description: Adds a Portfolio-tier level, the only tier that takes new levels, at the bottom of the tier; reorder it with `WorkTypeLevels_Reorder`. Level names must be unique. Returns the new level's integer id.

get.summary: Get work type level details using the id.

put.summary: Update a work type level.
put.description: Renames a level of any tier or changes its description; its tier and order do not change here. Level names must be unique. `id` must match `id` in the body. A whole-record overwrite: an omitted description is cleared, so read the level first and pass back what should stay.

put.summary: Update the order of portfolio tier work type levels.
put.description: `levels` maps each Portfolio-tier level's id to its new position, 1 being the top, as a JSON object: `{ "levels": { "12": 1, "14": 2 } }`. Only Portfolio-tier levels can be reordered. Levels left out keep their position, and the call is refused if two Portfolio levels would end up at the same position, so send every level whose position changes.

get.summary: Get a list of all work types.
get.description: The kinds of work item, such as Epic, Feature, User Story or Bug, by name, each with an integer `id` and its `level`, which sets its tier (Portfolio, Requirement, Task or Other) and so where its work items appear. Active work types only unless `includeInactive` is true.

post.summary: Create a work type.
post.description: Returns the new work type's integer id. The name must be unique and can never be changed; `levelId` is a work type level's id from `WorkTypeLevels_GetWorkTypeLevels`.
