post.description: `orderedKpiIds` lists **every** KPI of the initiative exactly once, in the new display order; a partial list is rejected. Rejected once the initiative is completed or canceled. Confirm with the user before calling. Takes the initiative's UUID only, not a key.

get.summary: Get the checkpoints for a KPI — the dated milestones a KPI is expected to hit, each with its own target value and optional at-risk threshold.
get.description: Returns the checkpoint definitions only, without the measurements taken against them; use StrategicInitiatives_GetKpiCheckpointPlan for both together.

get.summary: Get the checkpoint plan for a KPI: every checkpoint paired with the measurement recorded against it, plus a computed health and trend per checkpoint.
get.description: This is the best single call for assessing whether a KPI is on track over time. A checkpoint with no measurement has a null measurement, health, and trend.

post.summary: Replace a KPI's checkpoint plan — the dated targets it is expected to hit.
post.description: **The body is the whole plan**: a checkpoint with a `checkpointId` updates that existing checkpoint, one without is added, and every existing checkpoint left out is removed. Read the plan first (StrategicInitiatives_GetKpiCheckpoints) and send back each checkpoint to keep with its id. Each checkpoint has a `targetValue`, a `checkpointDate` (ISO 8601 UTC datetime, unique within the KPI), a short `dateLabel` such as "Q1 2027" (at most 16 characters), and an optional `atRiskValue` threshold that must differ from the target. Measurements are not changed. `strategicInitiativeId` and `kpiId` in the body must match the path parameters. Confirm with the user before calling, naming any checkpoint that would be removed. Takes UUIDs only, not keys.

get.summary: Get every measurement recorded against a KPI, each with its actual value, the date it was taken, who took it, and an optional note.

post.summary: Record a measurement against a KPI — the actual observed value at a point in time.
post.description: Measurements accumulate as a history rather than overwriting; the KPI's headline actual value is the measurement with the latest measurementDate. Measurement dates must be unique within a KPI, so re-submitting an existing date is rejected rather than treated as an update. strategicInitiativeId and kpiId in the body must match the path parameters. Unlike the KPI read tools, this takes UUIDs only, not keys.

delete.summary: Remove a measurement from a KPI.
delete.description: This deletes the recorded history entry and changes the KPI's derived actual value and progress. To record a new observation, add a measurement instead — deletion is only for correcting a wrong entry, or for freeing up a date so it can be re-recorded.

get.summary: Get the projects linked to a strategic initiative — the delivery work carried out to achieve it.

post.summary: Set which projects are linked to a strategic initiative as the work delivering it.
post.description: **`projectIds` is the complete set**: projects not in it are unlinked and new ones are linked, so an empty list unlinks every project. Read the current links first (StrategicInitiatives_GetProjects) and include every project that should stay. Every id must be an existing project's UUID. Rejected once the initiative is completed or canceled. The `id` in the body must match the id path parameter. Confirm with the user before calling, naming any project that would be unlinked. Takes UUIDs only, not keys.

get.summary: Get a list of estimation scales.
get.description: Sorted by name. Each scale has an integer `id`, `name`, `description`, `isActive` and its ordered `values`. Only active scales are listed unless `includeInactive` is true. Requires the planning-poker feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

post.summary: Create a custom estimation scale.
post.description: `values` are the cards in the order they are shown: at least 2, each at most 32 characters. The new scale is active. Returns its integer id.

get.summary: Get estimation scale details.
get.description: Takes the scale's integer id. Returns the scale, active or not, with its ordered `values`.

put.summary: Update a custom estimation scale.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite: `name`, `description` and `values` are all set from the body, so an omitted `description` is cleared and `values` replaces the whole list. Read the scale with EstimationScales_GetScale first and pass back what should stay. Applies to any scale, including the ones Wayd seeds, and every session on the scale shows the new values, completed ones included. Takes the scale's integer id, in the path and again as `estimationScaleId` in the body.

delete.summary: Delete a custom estimation scale.
delete.description: Permanently deletes the scale. Refused while any poker session uses it, or when it is the last active scale; deactivate it with EstimationScales_SetActiveStatus instead. Takes the scale's integer id.

put.summary: Set the active status of an estimation scale.
put.description: `isActive` false takes the scale out of the default list, which is what new sessions are chosen from, without changing sessions that use it; true brings it back. Fails when the scale already has that status, and the last active scale cannot be deactivated. Takes the scale's integer id, in the path and again as `id` in the body.

get.summary: Get a list of planning intervals.

post.summary: Create a planning interval.
post.description: Iterations are generated from `iterationWeeks` and `iterationPrefix`: each is `iterationWeeks` long and named the prefix plus its sequence number, starting at `start`; the last one is cut to `end` and is an Innovation and Planning (IP) iteration, the rest Development. Change them afterwards with PlanningIntervals_ManageDates. The new interval has no teams (add them with PlanningIntervals_ManageTeams) and its objectives are unlocked. Returns the new interval's `id` and `key`.

get.summary: Get planning interval details.
Get a planning interval's activity history, newest first: every change recorded on the interval itself — details, dates, teams, iterations, sprint mappings, and objectives being locked or unlocked.
get.description: Each objective keeps its own history (`PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveActivities`). Each entry has a `category` (Created, Updated, ScheduleChanged, StatusChanged, StateChanged, Health, Removed, Baseline), an `actorKind` (User, System, Import, Sync, Anonymous) with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string. A change carries both ends, the value before and after. People in a payload are employee ids, not user ids. A Baseline entry marks where tracking began for a record that already existed, holding what it looked like then; nothing before it was recorded. An entry with `isRelated: true` was raised on another record and is listed here because it concerns this one; `raisedOn` names that record, or is null where it could not be resolved (typically removed since). Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

get.summary: Get the PI calendar.
Get the PI predictability for all teams.

post.summary: Submit a csv file of planning intervals to import. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.
post.description: One row is one planning interval, with the teams that ran it in a semicolon-separated TeamIds column. Iterations are generated from IterationWeeks and IterationPrefix; there is no column for them. Creates only — a row whose Name is already taken is rejected, so TeamIds never replaces an existing roster, and a blank TeamIds simply leaves the new interval with no teams.

put.summary: Update a planning interval's name, description and whether its objectives are locked.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite: every field is set from the body, so an omitted `description` is cleared and an omitted `objectivesLocked` unlocks the objectives. Read the interval with PlanningIntervals_GetPlanningInterval first and pass back what should stay. Takes the interval's UUID, in the path and again as `id` in the body. Locking objectives freezes the plan: no objective can be created or deleted, and an objective update keeps its name and stretch flag while its other fields stay editable. Dates and iterations change through PlanningIntervals_ManageDates, teams through PlanningIntervals_ManageTeams.

get.summary: Get a list of teams participating in a planning interval.
Get the PI predictability for a specific team.

post.summary: Set a planning interval's start and end dates and its complete list of iterations.
post.description: Replaces the iteration list: an iteration in `iterations` with its `iterationId` is updated, one without an `iterationId` is added, and an existing iteration left out is deleted along with its sprint mappings. Read the current iterations with PlanningIntervals_GetIterations first and pass back every one that should stay, with its id. Each iteration needs a `name` unique within the interval, a `categoryId` (1 Development, 2 Innovation and Planning; PlanningIntervals_GetIterationCategories lists them), and `start`/`end` inside the interval's dates that overlap no other iteration. Takes the interval's UUID, in the path and again as `id` in the body. Nothing changes when any rule fails.

post.summary: Set the complete list of teams taking part in a planning interval.
post.description: Replaces the roster: `teamIds` is every team that should take part, teams and teams of teams alike (UUIDs). A team left out is removed along with its sprint mappings; its objectives stay. Read the current roster with PlanningIntervals_GetTeams first and pass back every team that should stay. A Scrum team that joins has its sprints mapped automatically, each to the iteration holding most of its days. Takes the interval's UUID, in the path and again as `id` in the body. A team created moments ago may not have reached planning yet; the call then fails and can be retried.

get.summary: Get a list of iterations for a planning interval.
Get the capacity of each team in a planning interval, for the whole planning interval and each of its iterations.
get.description: Returns the planning interval's `iterations` in date order and, for each team in it, its capacity in person-days after holidays, time away and team days off: a `total` over the whole planning interval and one figure per iteration in `iterations`, each with `allocatedPersonDays` in every role, `deliveryPersonDays` in roles that count toward delivery capacity and `awayPersonDays` that time away took. Iterations are read by the planning interval's own dates, whatever a team's sprint length or cadence. A team of teams is counted as its rollup: its own allocations and those of the teams beneath it for the days they were in its hierarchy, so a team beneath it that is also in the planning interval is counted in both rows. A team's sprint days off count as nobody working, wherever that team is counted, and a team's are listed in `teamDaysOff`. `hasAllocations` is false for a team with nobody allocated in the planning interval. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get a specific planning interval iteration.
Get a list of iteration categories.
Get iteration sprint mappings for a Planning Interval.
get.description: Optionally filter by iterationId.

post.summary: Map team sprints to Planning Interval iterations.
post.description: This is a sync/replace operation that sets the complete desired state for the team's sprint mappings. `iterationSprintMappings` maps an iteration id to a sprint id, or to null to leave that iteration with no sprint for the team; every sprint of the team that is mapped now but not named as a value is unmapped, whether or not its iteration is in the body. So pass every mapping that should stay — read them with PlanningIntervals_GetIterationSprints first. A team has at most one sprint per iteration and a sprint maps to one iteration; mapping a sprint moves it from wherever it was. The team must take part in the interval, and each sprint must be one of that team's own sprints and of type Sprint; any other sprint refuses the whole request. All ids are UUIDs; the interval's and team's are given in the path and again as `id` and `teamId` in the body.

get.summary: Get PI-level metrics aggregated across all mapped sprints in every iteration.
get.description: Returns the interval's `teamCount` and `sprintCount` (teams and sprints with a sprint mapping), the `cycleTime` across every mapped sprint, and `teamMetrics`, one entry per team with its `teamCode`, `predictability`, regular, stretch and completed objective counts, `cycleTime` and `sprintCount`. Only sprint mappings count: a Kanban team, which has no sprints, is absent. A 404 when the interval is not found, or when a mapped sprint's team no longer resolves to a team with a code. For a single iteration's work figures use PlanningIntervals_GetIterationMetrics.

get.summary: Get metrics for a PI iteration aggregated across its mapped sprints and Kanban teams.
get.description: Each sprint in `sprintMetrics` is measured in its team's `sizingMethod` (StoryPoints, Effort, Size or Count), so its `*Estimate` fields are in that unit; the `*WorkItems` fields are always item counts. A Kanban team in the planning interval with no sprint mapped to the iteration has an entry in `dateMeasuredTeamMetrics` instead, measured by the iteration's dates in the team's time zone: Requirement-tier work completed (Done-category, not Removed) by done date within them, and work in progress at the iteration's end (from work item history; now for the current iteration). Work counts for the team an item is on now. A Kanban team has no scope, so it has no total or not-started figures and adds nothing to the iteration's `totalWorkItems` or `notStartedWorkItems`, while its completed, in-progress, unestimated and cycle-time figures are in the iteration's totals; take a completion rate from the sprint entries. `isHistoryIncomplete` marks a Kanban team whose past in-progress figure may be short because its workspace's history has not been read through. The iteration's `totalEstimate` and `notStartedEstimate` are in `sprintSizingMethod`, the sprints' shared unit; its `completedEstimate` and `inProgressEstimate` are in `sizingMethod`, the unit shared by its sprints and Kanban teams. Each is null, with its totals, when they use different sizing methods: estimates in different units are never added.

get.summary: Get combined backlog for a PI iteration from all mapped sprints.
Get the combined backlog for a PI from every sprint mapped to any of its iterations.
get.description: The work items of every mapped sprint in one list; a Kanban team's work, which is in no sprint, is not included. For one iteration's backlog use PlanningIntervals_GetIterationBacklog.

get.summary: Get a list of planning interval objectives.
get.description: Optionally filter by teamId.

get.summary: Get a planning interval objective.
Get a planning interval objective's activity history, newest first: every change recorded on the objective — details, status, progress, order, stretch, timeline and health checks.
get.description: The objective must belong to the planning interval named alongside it, or the call returns 404. Each entry has a `category` (Created, Updated, ScheduleChanged, StatusChanged, StateChanged, Health, Removed, Baseline), an `actorKind` (User, System, Import, Sync, Anonymous) with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string. A change carries both ends, the value before and after. People in a payload are employee ids, not user ids. A Baseline entry marks where tracking began for a record that already existed, holding what it looked like then; nothing before it was recorded. An entry with `isRelated: true` was raised on another record and is listed here because it concerns this one; `raisedOn` names that record, or is null where it could not be resolved (typically removed since). Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

post.summary: Create a planning interval objective.
post.description: Creates a team's objective: `teamId` is the UUID of a team or team of teams taking part in the interval (PlanningIntervals_GetTeams); any other team is refused. `name` is the commitment itself; `startDate` and `targetDate` are optional, and when both are given the start must be before the target. `order` is optional. A new objective is Not Started at 0% progress. Refused while the interval's objectives are locked. Takes the interval's UUID, in the path and again as `planningIntervalId` in the body. Returns the new objective's `id` and `key`.

put.summary: Update a planning interval objective.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite: name, description, status, progress, dates and stretch flag are all set from the body, so an omitted `description`, `startDate` or `targetDate` is cleared, an omitted `isStretch` becomes false and an omitted `progress` 0. Read the objective with PlanningIntervals_GetObjective first and pass back what should stay. `statusId` is a number: 1 Not Started, 2 In Progress, 3 Completed, 4 Canceled, 5 Missed (PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveStatuses lists them); Completed, Canceled and Missed close the objective. `progress` is 0 to 100. While the interval's objectives are locked, `name` and `isStretch` keep their current values whatever the body says; the rest still changes. Order is changed with PlanningIntervals_UpdateObjectivesOrder. Both ids are UUIDs, given in the path and again as `planningIntervalId` and `objectiveId` in the body.

delete.summary: Delete a planning interval objective.
delete.description: Removes the objective from the interval. Refused while the interval's objectives are locked. Both ids are UUIDs.

put.summary: Update the order of planning interval objectives.
put.description: `objectives` maps an objective's UUID to its new `order`, or to null to clear it; objectives not named keep their order. Every objective named must belong to the interval, or nothing changes. Takes the interval's UUID, in the path and again as `planningIntervalId` in the body.

get.summary: Get a health report for planning interval objectives.
get.description: Optionally filter by teamId.

get.summary: Get work items linked to a planning interval objective.
Forecast when a planning interval objective's linked work items will be done, by Monte Carlo simulation of each team's recent throughput and each work item's backlog position and open predecessors.
get.description: Returns an `outcome` (Forecast, Done, Not Enough History, Blocked by Dependency, Cannot Forecast, Nothing Remaining); on Forecast, completion `percentiles` (a `date` per `confidence`) and `chanceOfFinishingByTargetDate` (0 to 1) against `targetDate` when given, else the objective's target date, else the planning interval's end. `excludedWorkItems` could not be forecast (see `issues`), which makes the dates a lower bound; `dependencies` gives each predecessor's `shareOfTrialsSettingFinish`. Requires the delivery-forecasting feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get daily metrics for work items linked to a planning interval objective.

post.summary: Set the complete list of work items linked to a planning interval objective.
post.description: Replaces the links: `workItemIds` is every work item that should be linked (work item UUIDs, not keys); a linked item left out is unlinked and an empty list unlinks them all. Read the current links with PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveWorkItems first and pass back every one that should stay. Both ids are UUIDs, given in the path and again as `planningIntervalId` and `objectiveId` in the body; an objective not in the interval is a 404.

post.summary: Submit a csv file of planning interval objectives to import. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.
post.description: Each row names the planning interval it belongs to in PlanningIntervalId, so one file can cover many planning intervals.

get.summary: Get a list of all PI objective statuses.
Get everything needed to recommend a health check for a planning interval objective, in one read.
get.description: Use this before recommending or logging a PI objective health check, in place of calling PlanningIntervals_GetPlanningInterval, PlanningIntervals_GetObjective, PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveWorkItems, PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveWorkItemMetrics, PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveForecast, PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveHealthChecks, PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveActivities and PlanningIntervals_GetRisks one by one. Both ids accept a UUID or a key; an objective not in the planning interval is a 404. Returns the interval and objective; `schedule` with the effective `startDate` and `targetDate` (the interval's start or end when the objective has none, flagged `startDateDefaulted` / `targetDateDefaulted`) and `elapsedShare` of that window (0 to 1); the linked `workItems` by stack rank with their progress rollup and daily `workItemMetrics`; the delivery `forecast` against the effective target date, or null with `forecastUnavailableReason` when delivery forecasting is off; `healthChecks`, newest first; `sinceLastCheck` with the activity since the last check, the `progressAtLastCheck` and `progressChange` (percentage points), and `activityTruncated` when there is more; and `teamRisks`, the objective's team's open risks in this interval (closed ones too with includeClosedRisks=true) — risks link to a team, not to an objective. lookbackDays, ignoreDependencies and startedWorkFirst tune the forecast as on PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveForecast. Classify: Healthy when progress keeps pace with `elapsedShare`, flow is steady and the forecast chance of finishing by the target date is about 80% or more; AtRisk when progress lags the schedule, work in progress piles up, the chance is 50–80% or the 85% date slightly passes the target, or a dependency or risk threatens delivery; Unhealthy when progress has stalled, the chance is below 50%, the 85% date is far past the target or the interval's end, or the outcome is Blocked by Dependency. With no forecast, judge without it and say so. Draft a note (at most 1024 characters) citing this evidence and present the status, a future expiration no later than the interval's end, and the note. Logging is a separate PlanningIntervals_CreateObjectiveHealthCheck call, made only after the user confirms and only where that tool is listed.

get.summary: Get the full health check history for a planning interval objective, ordered newest first.

post.summary: Log a new health check on a planning interval objective.
post.description: Creating a new check automatically expires the previously active check (only one non-expired check can exist at a time). Note: the API requires planningIntervalObjectiveId in the body in addition to the objectiveId path parameter — they must match. To recommend a check, first gather the evidence with PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveHealthCheckEvidence: the objective's effective dates and elapsed share, its linked work items and daily flow, the forecast, previous checks, the changes since the last one, and the team's open risks. Healthy (1) when progress keeps pace with elapsed time, flow is steady and the forecast chance of finishing by the target date is about 80% or more; AtRisk (2) when progress lags the schedule, work in progress piles up, the chance is 50–80% or the 85% date slightly passes the target, or a dependency or risk threatens delivery; Unhealthy (3) when progress has stalled, the chance is below 50%, the 85% date is far past the target or the PI's end, or the outcome is Blocked by Dependency. Draft a note (at most 1024 characters) citing that evidence — progress since the last check, forecast confidence, concerns — with a future expiration no later than the PI's end. Present the status, the expiration, the note and its rationale, and call this only after the user confirms.

get.summary: Get a single planning interval objective health check by ID.

put.summary: Update a planning interval objective health check.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite of the check's `statusId` (1 Healthy, 2 AtRisk, 3 Unhealthy), `expiration` and `note`: an omitted `note` is cleared. Read the check with PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveHealthCheck first and pass back what should stay. `expiration` must be in the future, and an expired check cannot be changed — log a new one with PlanningIntervals_CreateObjectiveHealthCheck instead. All ids are UUIDs; the objective's and the check's are given in the path and again as `planningIntervalObjectiveId` and `id` in the body. A check not on that objective, or an objective not in the interval, is a 404. Returns the updated check.

delete.summary: Delete a planning interval objective health check.
delete.description: Removes the check from the objective's history, expired or not; it is not replaced, so deleting the active check leaves the objective with none until a new one is logged. All ids are UUIDs; a check not on that objective, or an objective not in the interval, is a 404.

get.summary: Get planning interval risks. The default value for includeClosed is false.
get.description: Optionally filter by teamId.

get.summary: Get a list of poker sessions.
get.description: Each entry has its `id`, `key`, `name`, `status` (Active or Completed), `facilitator` and `roundCount`. Pass `status` (Active or Completed) to list only those. Requires the planning-poker feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

post.summary: Create a poker session.
post.description: Starts an Active session, facilitated by the caller, that estimates on the scale `estimationScaleId` (an integer; EstimationScales_GetScales lists the active scales). The scale must be active; a session already on a scale that is later deactivated keeps working. It has no rounds yet; add them with PokerSessions_AddRound. Returns the new session's `id` and `key`.

get.summary: Get poker session details using the Id or key.
get.description: Takes the session's UUID or key. Returns the session with its estimation scale and values, and its `rounds` in order, each with its `label`, `status` (Voting, Revealed or Accepted), `consensusEstimate`, `voteCount` and `votes` (participant and value). While a round is Voting, every vote's `value` is an empty string except the caller's own, so it shows who has voted but not what; values appear once the round is Revealed.

put.summary: Update a poker session.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite of `name` and `estimationScaleId`: pass the current scale id to keep it, even if that scale has since been deactivated. The scale can change only while the session has no rounds, and only to an active scale. A completed session cannot be updated. Takes the session's UUID.

delete.summary: Delete a poker session.
delete.description: Permanently deletes the session with all its rounds, votes and consensus estimates, whatever its status. To close a finished session but keep its results, use PokerSessions_CompleteSession. Takes the session's UUID.

put.summary: Complete a poker session.
put.description: Moves an Active session to Completed. A completed session is read-only (no rounds, votes, reveals, resets, consensus or label changes) and cannot be reopened. Takes the session's UUID.

post.summary: Add a round to a poker session.
post.description: A round is one item being estimated; `label` (optional, at most 512 characters) names it, such as a story's title or key. The round opens in Voting, after the session's other rounds. The session must be Active. Takes the session's UUID. Returns the new round.

delete.summary: Remove a round from a poker session.
delete.description: Deletes the round with its votes and consensus estimate. The session must be Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

put.summary: Reveal votes for a round.
put.description: Moves a round from Voting to Revealed, showing every vote; voting stays closed until the round is reset. The session must be Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

put.summary: Reset a round to allow re-voting.
put.description: Clears every vote and any consensus estimate and moves the round back to Voting, from Voting, Revealed or Accepted. The session must be Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

put.summary: Set the consensus estimate for a round.
put.description: Records the agreed `estimate` (at most 32 characters, normally one of the scale's values) and moves the round from Revealed to Accepted; the round must have been revealed. To change an accepted estimate, reset the round and vote again. The session must be Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

put.summary: Update the label for a round.
put.description: Replaces the round's `label`; an omitted or null label clears it. The session must be Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

post.summary: Submit a vote for a round.
post.description: Casts or replaces the caller's own vote; a vote is always the signed-in user's, never someone else's. `value` must be one of the session's scale values exactly as the scale lists them, special cards such as `?` included (read them with PokerSessions_GetSession); any other value is refused. The round must be Voting and the session Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

delete.summary: Withdraw a vote from a round.
delete.description: Removes the caller's own vote while the round is Voting; it fails when the caller has not voted. The session must be Active. Both ids are UUIDs.

get.summary: Get the risks of every team and team of teams.
get.description: Open risks only unless `includeClosed` is true. Each has its `id`, `key`, summary, owning `team`, status, ROAM category, `exposure` (Low, Medium or High, from impact and likelihood), assignee and follow-up date. For one team use Teams_GetRisks or TeamsOfTeams_GetRisks; for a planning interval, PlanningIntervals_GetRisks; for the caller's own, Risks_GetMyRisks.

post.summary: Create a risk for a team or team of teams.
post.description: `teamId` is the UUID of the owning team or team of teams (required). `categoryId` is the ROAM category's numeric id from Risks_GetCategories (1 Resolved, 2 Owned, 3 Accepted, 4 Mitigated); `impactId` and `likelihoodId` are grade ids from Risks_GetGrades (1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High). `assigneeId` is an employee UUID; `followUpDate` is yyyy-MM-dd; `response` is what is being done about it. The risk starts Open, reported now by the caller, whose account must be linked to an employee. Returns the new risk's `id` and `key`.

get.summary: Get risk details using the Id or key.
get.description: Takes the risk's UUID or integer key. Returns its description, owning team, reporter, `response` (what is being done about it), follow-up and closed dates. Status, category, impact, likelihood and exposure each come as `{ id, name }`; the `id` is what Risks_Update takes.

get.summary: Get a risk's activity history, newest first: its creation, detail changes, category, assessment (impact and likelihood), assignee and follow-up date changes, and closing or reopening.
get.description: Takes the risk's UUID or integer key. Each entry has a `category`, an `actorKind` with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string, carrying the value before and after a change. People in a payload are employee ids. Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

get.summary: Get a list of open risks assigned to me.
get.description: Scoped to the caller — no user parameter. Open risks whose assignee is the employee linked to the caller's account; empty when the account has no linked employee.

put.summary: Update a risk, including closing or reopening it.
put.description: **This is a whole-record overwrite: an omitted description, assignee, follow-up date or response is cleared.** Read the risk first with Risks_GetRisk and pass back what should stay. Takes the risk's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `riskId`. `teamId` must be the risk's current team; a risk cannot be moved to another team. `statusId` is 1 Open or 2 Closed (Risks_GetStatuses); closing stamps the closed date and reopening clears it. `categoryId`, `impactId` and `likelihoodId` are as for Risks_Create.

post.summary: Submit a csv file of risks to import. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.

get.summary: Get a list of all risk statuses.
get.description: Open and Closed, each with the numeric `id` the risk update tools take as `statusId`.

get.summary: Get a list of all risk categories.
get.description: The ROAM categories — Resolved, Owned, Accepted, Mitigated — each with the numeric `id` the risk tools take as `categoryId` and a description of when it applies.

get.summary: Get a list of all risk grades.
get.description: Low, Medium and High, each with the numeric `id` the risk tools take as `impactId` and `likelihoodId`. A risk's exposure is derived from the two: their ids summed below 4 is Low, exactly 4 Medium, above 4 High.

get.summary: Get a list of roadmaps.

post.summary: Create a roadmap.
post.description: `roadmapManagerIds` are employee UUIDs and must include the caller's own employee: only roadmap managers can change a roadmap. `visibilityId` is 1 Public (everyone can see it) or 2 Private (only its managers can); Roadmaps_GetVisibilityOptions lists them. `start` must be on or before `end`. The new roadmap is Active and has no items. Returns its `id` and `key`.

get.summary: Get roadmap details.

post.summary: Copy an existing roadmap.
post.description: Creates a new Active roadmap with the source's description, dates and every item (activities, timeboxes and milestones, with their nesting, colors and order), under the given `name`, `roadmapManagerIds` and `visibilityId` (1 Public, 2 Private). The source's color legend is not copied. `sourceRoadmapId` is the source's UUID; it must be public or managed by the caller. `roadmapManagerIds` are employee UUIDs and must include the caller's own employee. The source is unchanged. Returns the copy's `id` and `key`.

put.summary: Update a roadmap.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite of the name, description, dates, managers and visibility: an omitted `description` is cleared and `roadmapManagerIds` replaces the managers, so leaving a manager out removes them. Read the roadmap with Roadmaps_GetRoadmap first and pass back what should stay. The managers must include the caller's own employee, and only a manager can update. `visibilityId` is 1 Public or 2 Private. An archived roadmap cannot be changed; reactivate it first. Takes the roadmap's UUID, in the path and again as `id` in the body.

delete.summary: Delete a roadmap.
delete.description: Permanently deletes the roadmap and all its items. Only a manager can delete it, and an archived roadmap must be reactivated first; to retire a roadmap but keep it, use Roadmaps_ArchiveRoadmap instead. Takes the roadmap's UUID.

put.summary: Update the configured colors for a roadmap.
put.description: Replaces the roadmap's color legend: `colors` is the complete set, each a hex `color` (e.g. #4096FF) with a caption `name` (at most 32 characters), an `order` and `isDefault`; a color left out is removed and an empty list clears the legend. At most 30 colors, at most one default, no color value twice. Items keep their own colors. Read the current legend with Roadmaps_GetRoadmap first. Only a manager of an active roadmap can change it. Takes the roadmap's UUID, in the path and again as `roadmapId` in the body.

post.summary: Archive a roadmap.
post.description: Moves an Active roadmap to Archived, keeping it and its items; an archived roadmap is read-only until reactivated with Roadmaps_ActivateRoadmap. Only a manager can archive it. Takes the roadmap's UUID.

post.summary: Activate a roadmap.
post.description: Moves an Archived roadmap back to Active so it can be changed again. Only a manager can activate it. Takes the roadmap's UUID.

get.summary: Get all items (activities, timeboxes, milestones) for a roadmap.
Get roadmap activities.
Get roadmap item details.

post.summary: Create a roadmap item of type: Activity, Timebox, Milestone.
post.description: The body's `$type` picks the item type and must be its first property: "activity" or "timebox" with `start` and `end`, or "milestone" with `date`. Every type takes `roadmapId` (the roadmap's UUID, also in the path), `name`, and optional `description`, hex `color` and `parentId` — the UUID of an activity on the roadmap to nest the item under; only activities can be parents, and with no parent the item is top-level. Only a manager of an active roadmap can add items. Returns the new item's id.

put.summary: Update a roadmap item of type: Activity, Timebox, Milestone.
put.description: A whole-record overwrite: name, description, parent, color and dates are all set from the body, so an omitted `description` or `color` is cleared and an omitted `parentId` moves the item to the top level. Read the item with Roadmaps_GetItem first and pass back what should stay, or use Roadmaps_PatchItem to change only some fields. The body's `$type` must be its first property and match the item's type: "activity" or "timebox" with `start` and `end`, "milestone" with `date`. Both ids are UUIDs, given in the path and again as `roadmapId` and `itemId` in the body. Only a manager of an active roadmap can change it.

patch.summary: Partially update a roadmap item using JSON Patch (RFC 6902).
patch.description: Works for an Activity, Timebox or Milestone; the item keeps its type. Paths are the update's camelCase fields: /name, /description, /parentId, /color, plus /start and /end for an activity or timebox, or /date for a milestone. `replace` changes a field; a field the patch does not name keeps its value. Confirm with the user before calling.

delete.summary: Delete a roadmap item.
delete.description: Deleting an activity also deletes everything nested under it, at every level; read the roadmap with Roadmaps_GetItems first to see what goes with it. Both ids are UUIDs. Only a manager of an active roadmap can delete items.

put.summary: Update the date(s) on a roadmap item of type: Activity, Timebox, Milestone.
put.description: Changes only the item's dates, leaving its other fields as they are. The body's `$type` must be its first property and match the item's type: "activity" or "timebox" with `start` and `end`, "milestone" with `date`. Both ids are UUIDs, given in the path and again as `roadmapId` and `itemId` in the body. Only a manager of an active roadmap can change it.

put.summary: Update a roadmap activity's placement.
put.description: Places an activity at `order` (1-based) among its siblings under `parentId`, the UUID of another activity, or at the top level when `parentId` is null. With the activity's current parent this reorders it; with a different one it moves it there, renumbering both sets of siblings. Activities only — a milestone or timebox moves to another parent through Roadmaps_UpdateItem or Roadmaps_PatchItem. Both ids are UUIDs, given in the path and again as `roadmapId` and `itemId` in the body. Only a manager of an active roadmap can change it.

get.summary: Get a list of all roadmap visibility options.
Get a list of all roadmap states.
Get a list of story maps (id, key, name, description, status, owner).

post.summary: Create a story map.
post.description: Returns the new map's ID and key.

get.summary: Get a story map in full: goals, each with ordered steps and tasks (including checklists, persona tags, and linked work item IDs), plus the map's swim lanes and personas.

put.summary: Update a story map's name and description.

delete.summary: Delete a story map and everything on it.
delete.description: This is permanent — prefer StoryMaps_ArchiveStoryMap unless deletion is explicitly intended.

put.summary: Change the owner of a story map.
Archive a story map.

post.summary: Add a goal to a story map.
post.description: The goal is created empty; add its steps with StoryMaps_AddStep.

put.summary: Rename a goal.

delete.summary: Delete a goal, along with its steps and their tasks.

put.summary: Reorder a goal within the map.

post.summary: Add a step to a goal.

put.summary: Rename a step.

delete.summary: Delete a step and its tasks.

put.summary: Reorder a step within its goal.
Move a step into a different goal.

post.summary: Add a task (story card) to a step.
post.description: Without a swimLaneId, it lands in the default swim lane.

put.summary: Update a task's title and description.

delete.summary: Delete a task.

put.summary: Rename a task.
put.description: Updates only the title, leaving the description untouched. Prefer this over the combined update when editing one field, so a concurrent edit to the other is not reverted.

put.summary: Set a task's description.
put.description: Updates only the description, leaving the title untouched. Prefer this over the combined update when editing one field, so a concurrent edit to the other is not reverted.

put.summary: Move a task to a step and swim lane.
Set the personas tagged on a task.
put.description: Replaces the full set — pass every persona ID that should remain tagged. To tag one more persona, use StoryMaps_PatchTaskPersonas instead.

patch.summary: Tag or untag personas on a task with a JSON Patch (RFC 6902), keeping the tags it does not name.
patch.description: Prefer this to the matching Set*Personas tool for tagging or untagging a few personas. The path is /personaIds, holding persona ids from the map's personas. `add` with `/personaIds/-` tags one more persona; to untag, `replace` /personaIds with the set that should remain — never remove by index. Confirm with the user before calling.

post.summary: Add a checklist item to a task.
post.description: Returns the updated task.

put.summary: Rename a checklist item.

delete.summary: Remove a checklist item from a task.

put.summary: Check or uncheck a checklist item.

post.summary: Promote a checklist item into its own task in the same step.
post.description: Returns the new task.

put.summary: Link a task to an existing work item. A work item can be linked to at most one task per map.

delete.summary: Unlink a task from its work item.

post.summary: Add a swim lane, appended below the existing ones.

put.summary: Rename a swim lane. The default swim lane cannot be renamed.

delete.summary: Remove a swim lane.
delete.description: Its tasks return to the default swim lane; the response is the number of tasks moved.

put.summary: Set a swim lane's descriptive start and end dates.
put.description: Pass null to clear a date.

put.summary: Reorder a swim lane. The default swim lane cannot be reordered.

post.summary: Define a persona on the map.

put.summary: Update a persona's name, description, and color.

delete.summary: Delete a persona and strip its tag from every goal, step, and task.
delete.description: The response is the number of nodes untagged.

put.summary: Reorder a persona within the map's persona list.
Set the personas tagged on a goal.
put.description: Replaces the full set — pass every persona ID that should remain tagged. To tag one more persona, use StoryMaps_PatchGoalPersonas instead.

patch.summary: Tag or untag personas on a goal with a JSON Patch (RFC 6902), keeping the tags it does not name.
patch.description: Prefer this to the matching Set*Personas tool for tagging or untagging a few personas. The path is /personaIds, holding persona ids from the map's personas. `add` with `/personaIds/-` tags one more persona; to untag, `replace` /personaIds with the set that should remain — never remove by index. Confirm with the user before calling.

put.summary: Set the personas tagged on a step.
put.description: Replaces the full set — pass every persona ID that should remain tagged. To tag one more persona, use StoryMaps_PatchStepPersonas instead.

patch.summary: Tag or untag personas on a step with a JSON Patch (RFC 6902), keeping the tags it does not name.
patch.description: Prefer this to the matching Set*Personas tool for tagging or untagging a few personas. The path is /personaIds, holding persona ids from the map's personas. `add` with `/personaIds/-` tags one more persona; to untag, `replace` /personaIds with the set that should remain — never remove by index. Confirm with the user before calling.

get.summary: Get a list of all employees.
get.description: Returns active employees only unless `includeInactive` is true, sorted by last name. An employee is the person record that role, assignee and `employeeId` fields take, not a sign-in account. Each carries its UUID `id` (what those fields and the other employee tools take), integer `key`, employee number, email, job title, department and `manager`. Call it once and filter the result to resolve names to ids.

post.summary: Create an employee.
post.description: Adds an active person record by hand, for someone no people connector syncs. Creates no sign-in account. `employeeNumber` must be unique across employees. `managerId` is another employee's UUID; one that matches no employee is refused. Returns the new employee's id and key.

get.summary: Get employee details using the Id or key.
get.description: Takes the employee's UUID `id` or integer `key`; the other employee tools take the UUID only. Returns the name parts, every email address the person is known by, employee number, hire date, job details, `manager` and `isActive`, active or not.

post.summary: Import employees from a csv file. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.

put.summary: Update an employee.
put.description: This is a whole-record overwrite: every field is set from the request body, so an omitted field is cleared — including `managerId`, which removes the manager. Read the employee first and send back every value that should stay. The `id` in the body must match the path. `employeeNumber` must stay unique, and a `managerId` that matches no employee is refused. Does not change whether the employee is active. An employee synced by a people connector is overwritten from the source system at its next sync.

delete.summary: Delete an employee.
delete.description: Permanently deletes the employee record by UUID; returns 404 when no employee has the id. A people connector recreates an employee it still syncs at its next sync; to remove a synced record that should not exist, use Employees_RemoveInvalid instead.

get.summary: Get a list of direct reports for an employee.
get.description: Takes the manager's UUID `id` and returns the active employees whose manager they are, sorted by last name: one level only, not the whole reporting tree. An unknown id returns an empty list.

post.summary: Remove invalid employee record from employee list.
post.description: For a record a people connector synced that is not a real employee, such as a shared mailbox or service account. Clears the manager of its direct reports, deletes the employee, and blocks its employee number so the connector never brings it back; no tool undoes the block.

get.summary: Get team memberships for an employee.
get.description: Takes the employee's UUID `id` and returns one entry per team or team of teams they belong to, sorted by team name, each with the team and the member roles they hold on it. Membership is not allocation: Employees_GetAllocations says how much of their time each team has. Returns 404 when no employee has the id.

get.summary: Get how an employee's time is allocated to teams over time.
get.description: Returns every allocation across all teams in date order: the team, the role the time is spent in when one was chosen, the date range (`end` is null when it has no end) and the `percent` of the employee's time. An employee's allocations never add up to more than 100% on any day. `canManage` says whether the caller may change that team's allocations. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or no employee has the id.

put.summary: Set the share of an employee's time one or more teams have over date ranges.
put.description: Each change replaces what its team and role have over its date range and leaves other days as they were, so a change inside a longer allocation splits it; a `percent` of 0 ends the allocation for the range. The changes apply together or not at all, and fail if any day would then exceed 100% across all teams. The caller must be a member of every team named, or of its team of teams, unless they hold the Administer Teams permission. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or no employee has the id.

post.summary: Move a share of an employee's time from one team and role to another over a date range.
post.description: Lowers the source and raises the target by `percent` on every day of the range as one change, so a fully allocated employee can be moved between teams. Fails if the source has less than `percent` on any day of the range. The caller must be a member of both teams, or of their teams of teams, unless they hold the Administer Teams permission. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or no employee has the id.

get.summary: Get the reasons time away can be recorded for.
get.description: Each reason's `code` is what a stretch of time away carries and what the time away requests accept. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get when an employee is away and the holiday calendar they take.
get.description: Returns each stretch of time away in date order with the share of each day it takes (`percentAway`), and the holiday calendar the employee follows when it is not the system default. Time away lowers the employee's availability to every team they are allocated to and never counts toward their 100% allocation. `canManage` says whether the caller may record this employee's time away: the employee, anyone they report up to, and holders of the Administer Employee Time Away permission. Each stretch's `reason` is null unless `canManage` is true. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or no employee has the id.

post.summary: Record an employee as away for a stretch of days.
post.description: Records the employee as away from every team they are allocated to for `percentAway` of each day from `start` to `end`. Stretches may overlap, but a day cannot add up to more than a whole day away. Needs no permission: allowed for the employee, anyone they report up to, and holders of the Administer Employee Time Away permission, and the caller must be linked to an employee. Returns the id of the time away. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off. No employee having the id returns 404 to a caller allowed to manage any employee's time away and the same refusal as any other employee to everyone else.

put.summary: Change a stretch of an employee's time away.
put.description: Changes its days, the share of each day it takes, or its reason. This is a whole-record overwrite: `start`, `end`, `percentAway` and `reason` are all set from the body, so read the stretch with Employees_GetTimeAway first and send back the values that should stay. Takes the employee's UUID and the stretch's `id`. Allowed for the same people as recording it. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off. No employee having the id returns 404 to a caller allowed to manage any employee's time away and the same refusal as any other employee to everyone else.

delete.summary: Remove a stretch of an employee's time away.
delete.description: The employee counts as available on those days again. Allowed for the same people as recording it, whether or not the employee is still active. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off. No employee having the id returns 404 to a caller allowed to manage any employee's time away and the same refusal as any other employee to everyone else.

put.summary: Set the holiday calendar an employee follows.
put.description: Calendars are shared: assign the one for where the employee works, such as their country's. They take its holidays instead of the system default's, on every team they are allocated to; with none (`holidayCalendarId` null) they follow the system default. A team's own calendar never decides a person's holidays. Employees_GetTimeAway shows the calendar the employee follows now. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or no employee has the id.

put.summary: Set how many hours an employee's working day has.
put.description: For someone whose working day is shorter or longer than the system's, such as a part-timer contracted for 4 hours a day; with none (`workingDayHours` null) they have the system's. The same on every team. Their allocation is a share of this day, so a part-timer allocated in full adds 4 hours, half a person-day of an 8-hour system day, to a team's capacity; time away entered in hours is a share of it. Employees_GetTimeAway shows the employee's own and the system's working day. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off or no employee has the id.

get.summary: Get the work items assigned to an employee.
get.description: Takes the employee's UUID `id` and returns the backlog-level (Requirement tier) work items assigned to them across every workspace; epics, features and tasks are left out. `statusCategories` narrows them to any of the codes `Proposed`, `Active`, `Done` and `Removed`. `doneFrom` and `doneTo` keep only work items finished in that window, so either one leaves out work not yet done; a time without a zone is read as UTC. Needs the Work Items view permission.

get.summary: Get the holiday calendars, by name.
get.description: Each calendar has its `id` (UUID), `key`, name, description, `holidayCount`, and `isDefault` for the system default calendar, which a team operating model or employee with no calendar of its own takes.

post.summary: Create a holiday calendar with no holidays.
post.description: `name` is unique across calendars. Add its days with HolidayCalendars_AddHoliday, then assign it to a team through its operating model (Teams_SetOperatingModel or Teams_UpdateOperatingModel) or to a person with Employees_ChangeHolidayCalendar. Returns the new calendar's `id` (UUID) and `key`.

get.summary: Get a holiday calendar with its holidays.
get.description: Takes the calendar's UUID or integer key. Returns its `holidays` (each with its own `id`, `date` and `name`), `isDefault`, and how many team operating models (`operatingModelCount`) and employees (`employeeCount`) use it.

get.summary: Get a holiday calendar's activity history, newest first: its creation, detail changes, and holidays being added, changed or removed.
get.description: Takes the calendar's UUID or integer key. Each entry has a `category`, an `actorKind` with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string, carrying the value before and after a change. Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

put.summary: Rename a holiday calendar or change its description.
put.description: **This is a whole-record overwrite of both fields: an omitted description is cleared.** Takes the calendar's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `id`. `name` is unique across calendars. Its holidays have their own tools.

delete.summary: Delete a holiday calendar with its holidays.
delete.description: Takes the calendar's UUID `id`. Refused while it is the system default, or while any team operating model, past or current, or any employee uses it: HolidayCalendars_GetHolidayCalendar gives the counts. Cannot be undone, so confirm with the user before calling.

post.summary: Add a holiday to a calendar.
post.description: Takes the calendar's UUID `id`, a `date` (yyyy-MM-dd) and a `name`. A calendar holds at most one holiday per date. Every team and person taking the calendar loses that day from their capacity. Returns the new holiday's id.

put.summary: Move a holiday to another date or rename it.
put.description: Takes the calendar's UUID `id` and the holiday's `holidayId` from HolidayCalendars_GetHolidayCalendar. Both `date` and `name` are required and overwrite the holiday's; the new date must not already have a holiday in the calendar.

delete.summary: Remove a holiday from a calendar.
delete.description: Takes the calendar's UUID `id` and the holiday's `holidayId` from HolidayCalendars_GetHolidayCalendar. The day becomes a working day again for everyone taking the calendar.

get.summary: Get a list of team member roles.
get.description: The roles a person can hold on a team or team of teams, such as Developer or Scrum Master, by name. Active roles only unless `includeInactive` is true. Each has its UUID `id` (what the team member tools take as `roleIds`), `key`, name, description, `isActive`, and `countsTowardDeliveryCapacity`: whether time allocated in the role adds to a team's delivery capacity.

post.summary: Create a team member role.
post.description: `name` is unique across roles. `countsTowardDeliveryCapacity` defaults to true; set it false for a role, such as a manager's, whose time on a team does not burn its planned work. The role starts active. Returns the new role's UUID.

get.summary: Get a team member role by id.
get.description: Takes the role's UUID `id`.

put.summary: Update a team member role.
put.description: Takes the role's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `id`. **`name` and `description` are overwritten: an omitted description is cleared**; an omitted `countsTowardDeliveryCapacity` is left as it is. Changing `countsTowardDeliveryCapacity` changes every team's delivery capacity for time allocated in the role, past and future.

delete.summary: Delete a team member role.
delete.description: Takes the role's UUID `id`. Refused while any team member holds the role or any allocation uses it; deactivate it instead with TeamMemberRoles_Deactivate.

put.summary: Activate a team member role.
put.description: Takes the role's UUID `id`. Makes a deactivated role listed and offered again.

put.summary: Deactivate a team member role.
put.description: Takes the role's UUID `id`. The role drops out of TeamMemberRoles_GetList (unless `includeInactive`) and of allocation proposals; members who hold it keep it.

get.summary: Get a list of teams.

post.summary: Create a team.
post.description: `name` and `code` are each unique across teams and teams of teams; `code` is 2 to 10 uppercase letters and digits. `activeDate` (yyyy-MM-dd) is the day the team starts. The team starts with a Kanban, Count-sized operating model in the system default time zone and working week; change it with Teams_SetOperatingModel. To place it under a team of teams, call Teams_AddTeamMembership; to staff it, Teams_AddMember. Returns the new team's `id` (UUID) and `key` (integer).

get.summary: Get team details.

put.summary: Update a team's name, code and description.
put.description: **This is a whole-record overwrite of those three fields: an omitted description is cleared.** Read the team first with Teams_GetTeam and pass back what should stay. Takes the team's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `id`. `code` is 2 to 10 uppercase letters and digits. The active date, operating model, members and team-of-teams membership each have their own tools.

get.summary: Get a team's activity history, newest first: the team's creation, detail changes, activation and deactivation, members joining, leaving or changing roles (by employee and role id), its membership in a team of teams being added, re-dated or removed, and operating models being set, corrected or removed.
get.description: Each entry has a `category` (Created, Updated, ScheduleChanged, StatusChanged, StateChanged, Health, Removed, Baseline), an `actorKind` (User, System, Import, Sync, Anonymous) with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string. A change carries both ends, the value before and after. People in a payload are employee ids, not user ids. A Baseline entry marks where tracking began for a record that already existed, holding what it looked like then; nothing before it was recorded. An entry with `isRelated: true` was raised on another record and is listed here because it concerns this one; `raisedOn` names that record, or is null where it could not be resolved (typically removed since). Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

post.summary: Submit a csv file of teams to import. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.
Submit a csv file of team staffing rows to import. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.
Import the team hierarchy (parent/child team memberships) from a csv file. Returns the run — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still queued or running.

put.summary: Deactivate a team.
put.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `id`, and the `inactiveDate` (yyyy-MM-dd), which must be after the team's active date. Refused when the team is already inactive, or when its latest team-of-teams membership has no end date or ends after `inactiveDate`: end or remove that membership first with Teams_UpdateTeamMembership or Teams_RemoveTeamMembership. No tool reactivates a team, so confirm with the user before calling.

get.summary: Get a team's memberships in teams of teams, past, current and future.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Each membership has its own `id` (the `teamMembershipId` the update and remove tools take), the `child` team and `parent` team of teams, `start` and `end` (yyyy-MM-dd; no end is open-ended), and a `state` (Past, Active or Future) as of today. A team belongs to at most one team of teams on any day. Returns 404 for an unknown team.

post.summary: Place a team under a team of teams for a date range.
post.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `teamId`, and the parent team of teams' UUID in `parentTeamId` (resolve it with TeamsOfTeams_GetList). `start` and optional `end` are yyyy-MM-dd; no `end` is open-ended. Both teams must be active, and the range must not overlap another of the team's memberships: to move a team, first end its current membership with Teams_UpdateTeamMembership, then add the new one starting the day after. The hierarchy drives team-of-teams rollups (capacity, work distribution) for those dates.

put.summary: Change the dates of a team's membership in a team of teams.
put.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the membership's `teamMembershipId` from Teams_GetTeamMemberships, each of which must match the body. **Both dates are overwritten: an omitted `end` makes the membership open-ended**, so pass the current `end` back to keep it. Both teams must be active, and the new range must not overlap the team's other memberships. The parent cannot be changed here: end this membership and add another.

delete.summary: Remove a team's membership in a team of teams.
delete.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the membership's `teamMembershipId` from Teams_GetTeamMemberships. The membership is deleted for its whole range, so the team drops out of the parent's rollups for past dates too; to record that a team left, end the membership with Teams_UpdateTeamMembership instead. Both teams must be active.

get.summary: Get a team's open backlog in rank order.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID or `code`. Returns the team's Requirement-tier work items (such as user stories and bugs) in a Proposed or Active status category, sorted by stack rank, each with its 1-based `rank`, `parentRank`, workspace, type, status, parent, sprint, assignee, project and its Story Points, Effort and Size estimates. Portfolio-tier items (epics, features) are not listed. An unknown team returns an empty list. To grade the backlog, use Teams_GetBacklogHealth.

get.summary: Grade a team's open backlog.
get.description: Returns `checks` — Runway, Net Flow and WIP Load measure the whole backlog; Stale, Old Proposed, Aging WIP, Missing Estimate, Oversized, No Parent, No Project, Unassigned Active, Carry-over, Closed Parent and Rank Inversion flag work items — each with an `outcome` (Assessed, Not Enough History, Not Applicable), a `grade` (Healthy, At Risk, Unhealthy; absent when not assessed), and a `value` (weeks, a ratio, active items per member, or the percent of in-scope work items flagged). `workItems` lists every open backlog work item in rank order with the `flags` that apply to it, and `thresholds` states the values it was graded with. Every threshold is optional and falls back to its default. Estimates (`totalEstimate`, `oversizedEstimate`, each work item's `estimate`) are in the team's current `sizingMethod` (StoryPoints, Effort or Size); a work item with no value in it is missing an estimate, and 0 is an estimate. For a team that sizes by Count, Missing Estimate and Oversized are Not Applicable.

parameters.name: LookbackDays
parameters.description: Days of history to measure throughput, cycle time and net flow over (14-365, default 90).

parameters.name: StaleDays
parameters.description: Days without a change before a work item is stale (default 90).

parameters.name: OldProposedDays
parameters.description: Days since creation before a proposed work item is old (default 180).

parameters.name: AgingWipPercentile
parameters.description: The cycle time percentile an active work item is aging beyond (default 85).

parameters.name: OversizedPercentile
parameters.description: The percentile of completed work's estimates, in the team's sizing method, a work item is oversized above (default 85).

parameters.name: ReadinessWindowWeeks
parameters.description: Weeks of throughput the readiness checks look ahead (default 4).

parameters.name: ReadinessFallbackItems
parameters.description: Top-ranked work items the readiness checks look at without enough history (default 20).

parameters.name: AtRiskPercent
parameters.description: Percent of work items flagged at which a check is At Risk (default 10).

parameters.name: UnhealthyPercent
parameters.description: Percent of work items flagged at which a check is Unhealthy (default 25).

parameters.name: RunwayAtRiskWeeks
parameters.description: Runway weeks below which the backlog is At Risk (default 4).

parameters.name: RunwayUnhealthyWeeks
parameters.description: Runway weeks below which the backlog is Unhealthy (default 2).

parameters.name: RunwayTooLongWeeks
parameters.description: Runway weeks above which the backlog is At Risk for being too long (default 26).

parameters.name: NetFlowAtRisk
parameters.description: Work items created per item completed above which net flow is At Risk (default 1.2).

parameters.name: NetFlowUnhealthy
parameters.description: Work items created per item completed above which net flow is Unhealthy (default 1.5).

parameters.name: WipLoadAtRisk
parameters.description: Active work items per member above which WIP load is At Risk (default 1.5).

parameters.name: WipLoadUnhealthy
parameters.description: Active work items per member above which WIP load is Unhealthy (default 2).

get.summary: Report where a team's completed work went.
get.description: Groups the Requirement-tier work items the team completed between `from` and `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, UTC, max 366 days) by portfolio, program, project, strategic theme or work type. Measures: Count, or StoryPoints (only work done while the team sized in story points; unestimated items excluded or filled from the team average). Work with no project is its own group.

parameters.name: From
parameters.description: The first day of completed work to include (yyyy-MM-dd, UTC).

parameters.name: To
parameters.description: The last day of completed work to include (yyyy-MM-dd, UTC).

parameters.name: Dimension
parameters.description: What to group work by (default Portfolio).

parameters.name: Measure
parameters.description: How to weigh each work item (default Count).

parameters.name: Unestimated
parameters.description: StoryPoints and TeamEffort: what to do with items that have no estimate in their team's sizing method (default Exclude).

parameters.name: ThemeCounting
parameters.description: Strategic theme only: how to credit a project with several themes (default SplitEvenly).

get.summary: Get the capacity of a team over a date range, from the time people are allocated to it.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 731 days), the `workingDays` in the range and each person allocated to the team with their person-days: `allocatedPersonDays` in every role, `deliveryPersonDays` in roles that count toward delivery capacity, and `elsewherePersonDays` allocated to other teams on the same days. One person-day is one person allocated in full for one working day. `roles` breaks the allocated time down by team member role, each line saying whether it counts toward delivery capacity, and adds up to `allocatedPersonDays`. Each person carries their `allocations` to this team with the `personDays` each is worth, and their `elsewhereAllocations` to other teams in the range. A working day is a day in the team's working week that is not one of its holidays. `canManage` says whether the caller may change the allocations, which is done per person with Employees_ChangeAllocations. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Report the capacity of a team over a date range.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 731 days), one `lines` entry per person and team member role allocated to the team. A line's `total` is in person-days: `allocatedPersonDays` over the team's working days, the part lost to `holidayPersonDays` and `timeAwayPersonDays`, what is left as `availablePersonDays`, and the part of that in roles that count toward delivery capacity as `deliveryPersonDays`. `interval` (`Week` or `Month`) also splits each line into `buckets`, in the order of the report's `buckets`. `teams` holds the team alone, as `nodeId` 0. `people` gives each person's time over the system default working days that the report does not count: `outsidePersonDays` allocated to other teams and `unallocatedPersonDays` allocated nowhere. Time away is reported as time lost, never why. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get the capacity of a team over a date range day by day, to plan against.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 366 days), the `capacity` the `capacity` endpoint (Teams_GetCapacity) returns for the same range, the `days` of the team's working week in the range, and for each person allocated to it their time day by day. Each person has a `rows` entry per team member role with the `days` that role has time allocated: the `percent` and the `personDays` it is worth after the holidays the person takes and their time away. Their own `days` list the working days on which something else decides their time: `isHoliday` in the calendar they take, `percentAway` (never why), and `elsewherePercent` allocated to other teams. A day left out of a list has none of it. `daysOff` (repeatable) are days the whole team is off beyond its working week and holidays, such as a sprint's team days off: yyyy-MM-dd for a full day, or yyyy-MM-dd:percent for part of one (`2026-10-01:50` is half the day). Each takes its share of everyone's time that day and is listed in `teamDaysOff`; a day keeps its percent, worth only the share the team works, so 0 person-days on a full day off. Nothing is stored per day: change a day or a week through the change allocations endpoint (Employees_ChangeAllocations), as a change over that range. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Propose allocations for a team from its members, without saving anything.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Returns one row per active member and active role they hold on the team, for allocations starting on `from` (yyyy-MM-dd). A row has no `end` unless the member already has a later allocation to it, in which case it ends the day before so that allocation is untouched; a member with time on it on `from` has no rows. `remainingPercent` is what is left of the member's time across all teams: 100 less their most allocated day from `from` to `end`. `percent` is that remainder split evenly between the member's roles. A member with nothing left is returned at 0, not left out. Nothing is saved: send the rows to keep to the change allocations endpoint (Employees_ChangeAllocations). Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Forecast how many of a team's open backlog work items it will finish from today through `targetDate`, by Monte Carlo simulation of its recent daily throughput.
get.description: Returns an `outcome` (Forecast, or Not Enough History when the team finished fewer than 10 backlog work items in the window), `backlogWorkItems` open today, `percentiles` — at each `confidence` the `workItems` count finished at least that often and `throughWorkItem`, the backlog work item that count reaches (active items first unless `startedWorkFirst` is false, then rank order) — and a `histogram` of trials by work items finished. Requires the delivery-forecasting feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get a team's Requirement-tier work items, optionally filtered by status category and done date.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID or `code`. Lists the team's Requirement-tier work items (such as user stories and bugs; never epics or features), ordered by stack rank. `statusCategories` (repeatable: Proposed, Active, Done, Removed) narrows them; omit it for all. `doneFrom` and `doneTo` are ISO 8601 date-times (UTC when no offset is given) bounding when an item reached Done, and leave out items that are not done. For the open backlog in rank order, use Teams_GetBacklog. An unknown team returns an empty list.

get.summary: Get the open dependencies for a team.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Lists the work item dependencies, not removed, where the team owns either end and the predecessor (`source`) is not yet done (state To Do or In Progress); `target` is the successor waiting on it. Each has a `state`, a `health` (Healthy, At Risk, Unhealthy) from the two items' status and planned sprints, and a `scope` (Intra-Team, Cross-Team, or Unknown when an end has no team). Returns 404 for an unknown team.

get.summary: Get a team's risks.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Open risks only unless `includeClosed` is true. Each has its `id`, `key`, summary, team, status, ROAM category, `exposure` (Low, Medium or High, from impact and likelihood), assignee and follow-up date. Returns 404 for an unknown team; a team of teams' risks are under TeamsOfTeams_GetRisks.

post.summary: Create a risk for a team.
post.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`, which must match the body's `teamId`. `categoryId` is the ROAM category's numeric id from Risks_GetCategories (1 Resolved, 2 Owned, 3 Accepted, 4 Mitigated); `impactId` and `likelihoodId` are grade ids from Risks_GetGrades (1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High). `assigneeId` is an employee UUID. The risk starts Open, reported now by the caller, whose account must be linked to an employee. The same as Risks_Create.

get.summary: Get one of a team's risks.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the risk's UUID or integer key in `riskIdOrKey`. Returns 404 when the risk belongs to another team. Status, category, impact, likelihood and exposure each come as `{ id, name }`; the `id` is what Teams_UpdateRisk takes.

put.summary: Update one of a team's risks, including closing or reopening it.
put.description: **This is a whole-record overwrite: an omitted description, assignee, follow-up date or response is cleared.** Read the risk first with Teams_GetRisk and pass back what should stay. Takes the team's UUID `id` and the risk's UUID `riskId`, which must match the body's `teamId` and `riskId`; the risk cannot be moved to another team. `statusId` is 1 Open or 2 Closed (Risks_GetStatuses); closing stamps the closed date and reopening clears it. `categoryId`, `impactId` and `likelihoodId` are as for Teams_CreateRisk. The same as Risks_Update.

get.summary: Get one of a team's operating models.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the model's UUID `operatingModelId` from Teams_GetOperatingModels. An operating model is how the team works from its `start` to its `end` (none while current): its `methodology` (Scrum or Kanban), `sizingMethod` (StoryPoints, Count, Effort or Size), IANA `timeZone`, `commitmentGraceDays`, `workingDays`, `holidayCalendar` (null for the system default), and for Kanban an optional reporting cadence (`cadenceWeeks` and `cadenceAnchor`).

put.summary: Correct one of a team's operating models for its whole period.
put.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the model's `operatingModelId`; any model, current or past, can be corrected, and its dates do not change. The corrected values apply to every date the model covers, so for a change that starts on a date use Teams_SetOperatingModel instead. **This is a whole-record overwrite: an omitted `holidayCalendarId` reverts to the system default and omitted `cadenceWeeks`/`cadenceAnchor` remove the cadence**; only an omitted `workingDays` keeps the model's own. Read the model first with Teams_GetOperatingModel and pass back what should stay. Field rules are as for Teams_SetOperatingModel.

delete.summary: Delete a team's current operating model, reinstating the one before it.
delete.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the current model's `operatingModelId`. Only the current model can be deleted, and never the team's only one; the previous model becomes current again with no end date. Use it to undo a model set by mistake.

get.summary: Get the operating model history for a team.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Every operating model the team has had, back to back by date; `isCurrent` marks the one in force now. See Teams_GetOperatingModel for the fields.

post.summary: Change how a team works from a date, by starting a new operating model.
post.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. The new model starts on `startDate` (yyyy-MM-dd), which must be after the current model's start; the current model is closed the day before. Use it for a real change of methodology, sizing, time zone, working week, holiday calendar or cadence from a date; to fix a model's values for its whole period, use Teams_UpdateOperatingModel. `methodology` is Scrum or Kanban; `sizingMethod` is StoryPoints, Count, Effort or Size; `timeZone` is an IANA id; `commitmentGraceDays` is 0 to 14. `workingDays` (day names such as Monday, at least one) carries over the current model's when omitted. `holidayCalendarId` is a calendar from HolidayCalendars_GetList, or null for the system default. `cadenceWeeks` (1 to 8) with `cadenceAnchor` (yyyy-MM-dd, the first day of one period) set a Kanban team's reporting cadence; omit both for none, and always for Scrum.
