Teams_GetOperatingModelDefaults gives the values to start from. Returns the new model's id.

get.summary: Get the current operating model for a team, or the model effective on a specific date.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. `asOfDate` is an ISO 8601 date (its calendar date is used); omit it for today. Returns 404 when the team has no model in force on that date, such as a date before it started.

get.summary: Get the operating models in force for several teams on one date.
get.description: `teamIds` (repeatable) are team UUIDs. `asOfDate` is an ISO 8601 date (its calendar date is used); omit it for today. Returns one model per team that had one in force that day; unknown teams, and teams with none that day, are left out.

get.summary: Get the values a new operating model for a team is pre-filled with.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. The time zone is the one the team's parent team of teams had in effect on the start date (yyyy-MM-dd), else the system default; the commitment grace period is the system default. Use it to fill Teams_SetOperatingModel when the user has not said otherwise.

get.summary: Check if a team has ever used the Scrum methodology.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. True when any of its operating models, past or current, is Scrum, which means it may have sprints to report on. Returns 404 for an unknown team.

get.summary: Get the sprints for a team.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Every sprint the team has, past, current and future, ordered by start date, each with its `state` (Future, Active or Completed) and sprint type. An unknown team, or a team of teams, returns an empty list. For velocity and predictability, use Teams_GetSprintMetrics.

get.summary: Get the team's active sprint
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. Returns the sprint in progress now, with its dates, sprint type and what the caller may do with it. Returns 404 when the team has no sprint in progress, or the id is not a team's: report that the team has no active sprint, not a failure, and use Teams_GetSprints to find its next or last one.

get.summary: Get the team's sprint metrics.
get.description: The team's velocity, predictability and say/do over its last completed standard sprints: each sprint's values, their average and their spread, by item count and in the team's sizing method. Non-standard sprints, sprints whose work item history is incomplete and sprints with nothing committed are left out and listed with the reason. sprintWindow is how many sprints to measure over (3 to 12); omit it for the organization's sprint window. Estimates are in the team's sizing method now; a sprint measured in an earlier one counts by item only. Returns 404 for an id that is not a team's, including a team of teams, which has no sprints of its own.

get.summary: Get the team's cadence velocity.
get.description: A Kanban team's velocity over its reporting cadence: the Requirement-tier work it completed (Done-category status, not Removed) in each recent period, by item count and in the sizing method of the period's operating model, with the average and spread across ended, whole periods. Periods follow each operating model's cadence in that model's time zone; a period cut short where an operating model changes the cadence, time zone or sizing method inside it is partial and left out of the averages, as is the current period. periodWindow is how many ended periods to measure over (3 to 12); omit it for the organization's sprint window. There is no commitment, so no predictability or say/do. A team with no cadence returns no periods. Returns 404 for an id that is not a team's, including a team of teams, which has no cadence.

get.summary: Get the functional organization chart for a given date.
get.description: The tree of teams of teams and teams active on `asOfDate` (an ISO 8601 date, its calendar date used; omit for today), placed by their memberships on that day: `organization` holds the top-level units, each with its `id`, `key`, `code`, `type` (Team or Team of Teams), `level` (0 at the top), `path` of codes and `children`; a team with no parent that day is at the top. `total` counts every unit and `maxDepth` is the deepest level. Teams only, not people: for members use Teams_GetMembers.

get.summary: Get the members of a team.
get.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`. One entry per person, by name, with the `employee` (`id` is the employee UUID the member tools take) and every team member `role` they hold on the team. Membership has no dates; the time people give the team is their allocation, under Teams_GetCapacity. An unknown team returns an empty list.

post.summary: Add a member to a team.
post.description: Takes the team's UUID `id`, the `employeeId` (employee UUID) and at least one `roleIds` entry: team member role UUIDs from TeamMemberRoles_GetList. The team and the employee must be active. Adding someone who is already a member adds the roles; a role they already hold on the team is refused. Membership does not allocate their time; that is Employees_ChangeAllocations.

put.summary: Update a team member's roles.
put.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the member's `employeeId`. **`roleIds` replaces the member's roles on the team**: roles left out are removed, so pass every role they should keep (at least one; to take them off the team, use Teams_RemoveMember). Read the current roles with Teams_GetMembers first.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a team.
delete.description: Takes the team's UUID `id` and the member's `employeeId`, and removes every role they hold on the team. Their allocations to the team are not changed; end those with Employees_ChangeAllocations.

get.summary: Get a list of teams of teams in the organization.

post.summary: Create a team of teams.
post.description: `name` and `code` are each unique across teams and teams of teams; `code` is 2 to 10 uppercase letters and digits. `activeDate` (yyyy-MM-dd) is the day it starts. It starts with an operating model in the system default time zone. To nest it under another team of teams, call TeamsOfTeams_AddTeamMembership; to put teams under it, call Teams_AddTeamMembership on each team. Returns the new team of teams' `id` (UUID) and `key` (integer).

get.summary: Get team of teams details using the key.
get.description: Takes the integer `key` (the parameter is named `id`), not the UUID; TeamsOfTeams_GetList returns both.

put.summary: Update a team of teams' name, code and description.
put.description: **This is a whole-record overwrite of those three fields: an omitted description is cleared.** Read it first with TeamsOfTeams_GetTeamOfTeams and pass back what should stay. Takes the UUID `id`, which must match the body's `id`. `code` is 2 to 10 uppercase letters and digits.

get.summary: Get a team of teams' activity history, newest first: its creation, detail changes, activation and deactivation, members joining, leaving or changing roles (by employee and role id), its own membership in a parent team of teams being added, re-dated or removed, and operating models being set, corrected or removed.
get.description: Takes the UUID or integer key. Each entry has a `category` (Created, Updated, ScheduleChanged, StatusChanged, StateChanged, Health, Removed, Baseline), an `actorKind` (User, System, Import, Sync, Anonymous) with the acting `employee` when there is one, a `timestamp`, a one-line `summary`, and a `payload`: the event's fields as a JSON string. A change carries both ends, the value before and after. People in a payload are employee ids, not user ids. A Baseline entry marks where tracking began for a record that already existed; nothing before it was recorded. Paged: the response carries `totalCount` and `hasNextPage`.

get.summary: Report where the completed work of a team of teams, and every team beneath it, went.
get.description: Groups the Requirement-tier work items completed between `from` and `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, UTC, max 366 days) by portfolio, program, project, strategic theme or work type. Each team's work rolls up to the parent it had on the day the work was done. Measures: Count, StoryPoints (only teams sizing in story points), or TeamEffort (each team's split in its own sizing method, StoryPoints, Effort, Size or Count, as on the day the work was done, combined by share of completed items; recommended for teams of teams). Work with no project is its own group.

parameters.name: From
parameters.description: The first day of completed work to include (yyyy-MM-dd, UTC).

parameters.name: To
parameters.description: The last day of completed work to include (yyyy-MM-dd, UTC).

parameters.name: Dimension
parameters.description: What to group work by (default Portfolio).

parameters.name: Measure
parameters.description: How to weigh each work item (default Count).

parameters.name: Unestimated
parameters.description: StoryPoints and TeamEffort: what to do with items that have no estimate in their team's sizing method (default Exclude).

parameters.name: ThemeCounting
parameters.description: Strategic theme only: how to credit a project with several themes (default SplitEvenly).

get.summary: Get the capacity of a team of teams over a date range, from the time people are allocated to it.
get.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 731 days), the `workingDays` in the range and each person allocated to the team of teams with their person-days: `allocatedPersonDays` in every role, `deliveryPersonDays` in roles that count toward delivery capacity, and `elsewherePersonDays` allocated to other teams on the same days. One person-day is one person allocated in full for one working day. `roles` breaks the allocated time down by team member role, each line saying whether it counts toward delivery capacity, and adds up to `allocatedPersonDays`. Each person carries their `allocations` to this team with the `personDays` each is worth, and their `elsewhereAllocations` to other teams in the range. It counts only people allocated to the team of teams directly, over the system default working week and holidays; `capacity/rollup` (TeamsOfTeams_GetCapacityRollup) adds the teams beneath it. `canManage` says whether the caller may change the allocations, which is done per person with Employees_ChangeAllocations. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get the capacity of a team of teams over a date range with the teams beneath it rolled up.
get.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 731 days), the time allocated to the team of teams directly plus the time allocated to every team beneath it, at any depth. `allocatedPersonDays` and `deliveryPersonDays` are the totals; `directAllocatedPersonDays` and `directDeliveryPersonDays` are the team of teams' own part, which is what the `capacity` endpoint returns in detail. `children` is the tree of teams beneath it. Each has the `periods` of the range it counts for (the days its membership of its parent covers, less any its parent was itself out of the hierarchy), its own `workingDays` within them, the `people` allocated to it with each allocation's `personDays` over those days, its direct figures, and its totals including its own `children`. A team is counted over its own working week and holidays, a team of teams over the system defaults, and a team with nothing allocated is still listed. A team that moved between two parents in the range appears under each for its days there. An allocation counts once, on the team it was made to, so a person allocated at two levels has time at each and none of it twice; `people` counts that person once. `roles` breaks the total down by team member role and adds up to `allocatedPersonDays`. Nothing is stored and nothing can be changed here: change a team's allocations through that team. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Report the capacity of a team of teams and every team beneath it over a date range.
get.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 731 days), one `lines` entry per person, team member role and team: the team of teams itself and every team beneath it at any depth, each counted only for the days it was in the hierarchy. A line's `total` is in person-days: `allocatedPersonDays` over the team's working days, the part lost to `holidayPersonDays` and `timeAwayPersonDays`, what is left as `availablePersonDays`, and the part of that in roles that count toward delivery capacity as `deliveryPersonDays`. `interval` (`Week` or `Month`) also splits each line into `buckets`, in the order of the report's `buckets`. `teams` lists the team of teams first (`nodeId` 0) and each team beneath it with its `parentNodeId`; a team that moved between two parents appears under each. `people` gives each person's time over the system default working days that the report does not count: `outsidePersonDays` allocated elsewhere and `unallocatedPersonDays` allocated nowhere. An allocation counts once, on the team it was made to, so every grouping of the lines gives `total`. Time away is reported as time lost, never why. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Get the capacity of a team of teams over a date range day by day, to plan against.
get.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id`. Returns, for `from` to `to` (yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, max 366 days), the `capacity` the `capacity` endpoint (TeamsOfTeams_GetCapacity) returns for the same range, the `days` of the system default working week in the range, and for each person allocated to it their time day by day. Each person has a `rows` entry per team member role with the `days` that role has time allocated: the `percent` and the `personDays` it is worth after the holidays the person takes and their time away. Their own `days` list the working days on which something else decides their time: `isHoliday` in the calendar they take, `percentAway` (never why), and `elsewherePercent` allocated to other teams. A day left out of a list has none of it. Nothing is stored per day: change a day or a week through the change allocations endpoint (Employees_ChangeAllocations), as a change over that range. Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

get.summary: Propose allocations for a team of teams from its members, without saving anything.
get.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id`. Returns one row per active member and active role they hold on the team of teams, for allocations starting on `from` (yyyy-MM-dd). A row has no `end` unless the member already has a later allocation to it, in which case it ends the day before so that allocation is untouched; a member with time on it on `from` has no rows. `remainingPercent` is what is left of the member's time across all teams: 100 less their most allocated day from `from` to `end`. `percent` is that remainder split evenly between the member's roles. A member with nothing left is returned at 0, not left out. Nothing is saved: send the rows to keep to the change allocations endpoint (Employees_ChangeAllocations). Requires the team-capacity-management feature flag; returns 404 when it is off.

put.summary: Deactivate a team of teams.
put.description: Takes the UUID `id`, which must match the body's `id`, and the `inactiveDate` (yyyy-MM-dd), which must be after its active date. Refused when it is already inactive, when its own latest membership in a parent has no end or ends after `inactiveDate`, or when the latest membership of a team beneath it has no end or ends after `inactiveDate`: end those memberships first. No tool reactivates it, so confirm with the user before calling.

get.summary: Get a team of teams' memberships: in its parent, and of the teams beneath it.
get.description: Takes the UUID `id`. Lists its own memberships in a parent team of teams first (where it is the `child`), then the memberships of the teams and teams of teams directly beneath it (where it is the `parent`), past, current and future. Each has its own `id` (the `teamMembershipId` the update and remove tools take), `start` and `end` (yyyy-MM-dd; no end is open-ended), and a `state` (Past, Active or Future) as of today. Change a child's membership through the child: Teams_UpdateTeamMembership for a team, TeamsOfTeams_UpdateTeamMembership for a team of teams. Returns 404 for an unknown team of teams.

post.summary: Nest a team of teams under another team of teams for a date range.
post.description: Takes the UUID `id` of the team of teams being nested, which must match the body's `teamId`, and the parent's UUID in `parentTeamId`. `start` and optional `end` are yyyy-MM-dd; no `end` is open-ended. Both must be active, the range must not overlap its other parent memberships, and the parent cannot be one of its own descendants. To put a team (not a team of teams) under it, use Teams_AddTeamMembership.

put.summary: Change the dates of a team of teams' membership in its parent.
put.description: Takes the UUID `id` of the team of teams that is the child and the membership's `teamMembershipId`, each of which must match the body. **Both dates are overwritten: an omitted `end` makes the membership open-ended**, so pass the current `end` back to keep it. Both must be active, and the new range must not overlap its other parent memberships.

delete.summary: Remove a team of teams' membership in its parent.
delete.description: Takes the UUID `id` of the team of teams that is the child and the membership's `teamMembershipId`. The membership is deleted for its whole range, so it drops out of the parent's rollups for past dates too; to record that it left, end the membership with TeamsOfTeams_UpdateTeamMembership instead. Both must be active.

get.summary: Get the operating model history for a team of teams.
get.description: Takes the UUID `id`. A team of teams' operating model holds only the IANA `timeZone` its own rollups count days in, from `start` to `end` (none while current); `isCurrent` marks the one in force now. It also seeds the time zone offered to teams beneath it (Teams_GetOperatingModelDefaults). Methodology, sizing and working weeks belong to teams.

post.summary: Change a team of teams' time zone from a date, by starting a new operating model.
post.description: Takes the UUID `id`. The new model starts on `startDate` (yyyy-MM-dd), which must be after the current model's start; the current model is closed the day before. `timeZone` is an IANA id. To fix the time zone for a model's whole period instead, use TeamsOfTeams_UpdateOperatingModel. Returns the new model's id.

get.summary: Get the values a new operating model for a team of teams is pre-filled with.
get.description: Takes the UUID `id`. The time zone is the one its parent team of teams had in effect on the start date (yyyy-MM-dd), else the system default.

get.summary: Get one of a team of teams' operating models.
get.description: Takes the UUID `id` and the model's UUID `operatingModelId` from TeamsOfTeams_GetOperatingModels.

put.summary: Correct an existing operating model for a team of teams.
put.description: Takes the UUID `id` and the model's `operatingModelId`; any model, current or past, can be corrected, and its dates do not change. Sets its IANA `timeZone`, the model's only value, for every date it covers.

delete.summary: Delete the current operating model from a team of teams.
delete.description: Takes the UUID `id` and the current model's `operatingModelId`. Only the current model can be deleted, and never the only one; the previous model becomes current again with no end date.

get.summary: Get a team of teams' own risks.
get.description: Takes the UUID `id`. Only risks raised on the team of teams itself, not those of the teams beneath it (Teams_GetRisks per team, or Risks_GetList for all). Open risks only unless `includeClosed` is true. Each has its `id`, `key`, summary, status, ROAM category, `exposure` (Low, Medium or High), assignee and follow-up date. Returns 404 for an unknown team of teams.

post.summary: Create a risk for a team of teams.
post.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id`, which must match the body's `teamId`. `categoryId` is the ROAM category's numeric id from Risks_GetCategories (1 Resolved, 2 Owned, 3 Accepted, 4 Mitigated); `impactId` and `likelihoodId` are grade ids from Risks_GetGrades (1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High). `assigneeId` is an employee UUID. The risk starts Open, reported now by the caller, whose account must be linked to an employee.

get.summary: Get one of a team of teams' risks.
get.description: Takes the team of teams' UUID `id` and the risk's UUID or integer key in `riskIdOrKey`. Returns 404 when the risk belongs to another team. Status, category, impact, likelihood and exposure each come as `{ id, name }`; the `id` is what TeamsOfTeams_UpdateRisk takes.

put.summary: Update one of a team of teams' risks, including closing or reopening it.
put.description: **This is a whole-record overwrite: an omitted description, assignee, follow-up date or response is cleared.** Read the risk first with TeamsOfTeams_GetRisk and pass back what should stay. Takes the team of teams' UUID `id` and the risk's UUID `riskId`, which must match the body's `teamId` and `riskId`; the risk cannot be moved to another team. `statusId` is 1 Open or 2 Closed (Risks_GetStatuses); closing stamps the closed date and reopening clears it. `categoryId`, `impactId` and `likelihoodId` are as for TeamsOfTeams_CreateRisk.

get.summary: Get the members of a team of teams.
get.description: Takes the UUID `id`. Only people who are members of the team of teams itself, not the members of the teams beneath it. One entry per person, by name, with the `employee` (`id` is the employee UUID the member tools take) and every team member `role` they hold. An unknown team of teams returns an empty list.

post.summary: Add a member to a team of teams.
post.description: Takes the UUID `id`, the `employeeId` (employee UUID) and at least one `roleIds` entry: team member role UUIDs from TeamMemberRoles_GetList. The team of teams and the employee must be active. Adding someone who is already a member adds the roles; a role they already hold here is refused.

put.summary: Update a team of teams member's roles.
put.description: Takes the UUID `id` and the member's `employeeId`. **`roleIds` replaces the member's roles here**: roles left out are removed, so pass every role they should keep (at least one; to remove them, use TeamsOfTeams_RemoveMember). Read the current roles with TeamsOfTeams_GetMembers first.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a team of teams.
delete.description: Takes the UUID `id` and the member's `employeeId`, and removes every role they hold here. Their allocations are not changed; end those with Employees_ChangeAllocations.

get.summary: Get a list of all team types.
get.description: The fixed kinds of team, in order: Team (people who work together on a prioritized backlog) and Team of Teams (a group of teams and other teams of teams). Each has a numeric `id`, `name` and `description`; a team's `type` names one of them.

get.summary: Get a list of links for a specific objectId.
Get a link by id.

put.summary: Update a link.

delete.summary: Delete a link.

post.summary: Create a link.

get.summary: List import runs, newest first, as `processes` with a `totalCount`.
get.description: Only runs of the kinds you may submit are included, or every kind if you hold View Imports. A run carries `status` (Queued, Processing, Cancelling, Succeeded, PartiallySucceeded, Failed, Cancelled), `isTerminal`, `isPreflight`, `atomicity` (PerRow; Atomic, where one rejected row means nothing is written; or PerGroup, where the rows sharing a group — named by `groupNoun`, such as every dependency of one product — apply together or not at all and the other groups are kept), and the counts `totalRowCount`, `succeededRowCount`, `failedRowCount` and `unappliedRowCount`. `canManage` says whether you may cancel, resume, retry or apply it.

get.summary: List the kinds of import you may see.
get.description: Each has its `key` (what `Imports_GetList` filters on), `displayName`, `atomicity` (PerRow; Atomic, where one rejected row means nothing is written; or PerGroup, where the rows sharing a group — named by `groupNoun`, such as every dependency of one product — apply together or not at all and the other groups are kept), `maxRows` and `preflightMaxRows` (the most rows one file may hold for each), and `canSubmit`, whether you may submit that kind of file and act on its runs.

get.summary: Get one import run's status and counts.
get.description: Poll this until `isTerminal` is true to follow a run that was still going when it was submitted. A run carries `status` (Queued, Processing, Cancelling, Succeeded, PartiallySucceeded, Failed, Cancelled), `isTerminal`, `isPreflight`, `atomicity` (PerRow; Atomic, where one rejected row means nothing is written; or PerGroup, where the rows sharing a group — named by `groupNoun`, such as every dependency of one product — apply together or not at all and the other groups are kept), and the counts `totalRowCount`, `succeededRowCount`, `failedRowCount` and `unappliedRowCount`. `canManage` says whether you may cancel, resume, retry or apply it. `error` explains a run that could not continue; a rejected row's reason is on the row, from `Imports_GetRows`.

get.summary: Get a page of an import run's row outcomes, as `rows` with a `totalCount`.
get.description: Each row has its `importId` (the file's ImportId column, or its position when that cell was blank), `rowNumber`, `status` (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled), the `error` a rejected row was refused for, any `warning` a successful row recorded, and `createdEntityId`. In a preflight, Succeeded means the row would have been imported. Filter by `status: Failed` to see only what needs fixing.

post.summary: Stop an import run that is still going.
post.description: A request, not an undo: the worker stops at its next batch boundary, and rows already applied stay applied. The rest can be picked up later with `Imports_Resume`. Refused for a run that has already finished.

post.summary: Queue a finished import run again to apply the rows it never reached — after it was stopped, or failed partway.
post.description: Rows that succeeded are never reapplied, and rejected rows stay rejected (use `Imports_RetryFailed` for those). Answers with `queuedRowCount` and `skippedRowCount`, the rows whose data the 30-day retention window already discarded. Refused for a run still going, and for a preflight, which is imported with `Imports_Apply` instead.

post.summary: Import, for real, the rows a finished preflight checked — without sending the file again.
post.description: Every row is submitted, including ones the preflight rejected, and each is checked again against the data as it is now, so the import may still refuse a row the preflight passed. Applying the same preflight twice rejects the records the first import created as duplicates, or, for an import with no natural key such as deployments, creates them a second time; check `appliedImportProcessId` on the preflight first. Refused once the preflight's rows pass the 30-day retention window. Answers with the new run once it has finished, or while it is still queued or running if it takes longer than a few seconds — check `isTerminal`, and poll `Imports_GetById` until it is true.

post.summary: Queue a finished import run again, reattempting its rejected rows as well as any it never reached.
post.description: Fix whatever the rows were rejected for first — the rows are resubmitted exactly as they were, so a problem in the file itself needs a corrected file instead. Rows that succeeded are never reapplied. Answers with `queuedRowCount` and `skippedRowCount`. Refused for a run still going, and for a preflight.

get.summary: Get the list of health check statuses.
Get the intake channels in the order requesters see them.
get.description: With `deskId`, only the active channels that desk offers, which may be none; `includeArchived` is then ignored.

post.summary: Add an intake channel to the end of the list.
post.description: Desks that offer every channel offer it at once; desks that chose their channels do not until a Desk Admin adds it.

put.summary: Rename an intake channel or change its description.
put.description: Every request carrying the channel reads the new name.

post.summary: Archive an intake channel.
post.description: No new request can be given an archived channel and no desk offers it; requests already carrying it keep it. Channels are archived, never deleted.

post.summary: Restore an archived intake channel.
post.description: Desks that offer every channel offer it again, as do desks that had chosen it before it was archived.

put.summary: Put the intake channels in the order requesters see them.
put.description: The list must name every channel, archived ones included, exactly once; a partial list is refused.

get.summary: Get the intake desks, or only those a requester can submit to now.

post.summary: Create an intake desk with its initial members.

get.summary: Get an intake desk.

put.summary: Update an intake desk's settings and members.
put.description: Needs a Desk Admin on the desk, who also chooses which company channels it offers. Changing its visibility, or naming, removing or re-roling a Desk Admin, needs the Demand Management Admin. A member removed while owning requests on the desk is unassigned from them. Send the desk's `revision` as `expectedRevision`: a desk changed since answers 409.

delete.summary: Delete an intake desk with no requests on it.
delete.description: A desk with requests on it cannot be deleted; close it instead. A desk changed while the delete was under way answers 409.

get.summary: Get the desk visibility values, with their codes.
Get the review workflow a desk's requests follow.
get.description: Whether the desk follows the organization's default, and whether you may choose another: a Desk Admin on it or the Demand Management Admin, while no request is on it.

put.summary: Point a desk at another published intake request workflow.
put.description: Needs a Desk Admin on the desk or the Demand Management Admin, and is refused while any request is on the desk. The desk then follows the chosen workflow rather than the organization's default.

get.summary: Get the published intake request workflows a desk can follow.
get.description: Building and editing workflows is in Settings, under status workflow administration.

get.summary: Get the roles a desk member can hold, with their codes.
Get the active employees a request can name, by name only.
get.description: For choosing a requester, a participant or whoever made a commitment, without the View permission on employees.

get.summary: Get the intake requests you can see, as summaries.
get.description: Without View, only requests on desks you are a member of and requests that are your own. Requests on a private desk are absent for anyone outside it rather than listed as redacted rows. With `mine`, only requests you are the requester of or submitted, including those entered on someone else's behalf. With `openOnly`, only requests still under review or accepted — in the Proposed or Active status category, whatever the desk's workflow calls the status.

post.summary: Submit an intake request to a desk.

get.summary: Get an intake request in the tiers you can read.
get.description: The summary is always returned; the substance is null when you may not read it.

get.summary: Get an intake request's history, limited to the tiers you can read.

put.summary: Update an intake request.
put.description: The requester can edit their own request while it is proposed; otherwise you must be an agent on the request's desk. You must also be able to read the request's detail.

delete.summary: Delete an intake request.
delete.description: Needs a Desk Admin on the request's desk. Deleting is a last resort: withdrawing or declining keeps a request on record.

put.summary: Give an intake request a different assignee, or unassign it.
put.description: Needs an agent on the request's desk. The assignee must be a member of that desk.

post.summary: Move an open intake request to another desk.
post.description: Needs an agent on the request's current desk; the destination need not be one you work, but must be open to new requests. A move to a less private desk is refused unless `confirmWiderVisibility` is set. An assignee who is not a member of the destination is unassigned.

get.summary: Get the statuses an intake request can arrive in on another desk.
get.description: The destination workflow's open statuses that need no reason, in its order, and the one the request arrives in unless you choose. Empty unless you can move the request: an agent on its current desk.

post.summary: Move an intake request to another status of its desk's workflow.
post.description: Needs an agent on the request's desk. Declining, deferring, marking a duplicate and finishing need a `reason` the requester can read; marking a duplicate needs `duplicateOfId`, a request you can see that is not itself a duplicate. Withdrawn is the requester's, through withdraw.

post.summary: Withdraw your own open intake request.
post.description: Only the request's requester; the submitter cannot withdraw a request entered on someone's behalf.

get.summary: Get the statuses you can move an intake request to, with what each move needs.
get.description: In its desk workflow's order, without the status it holds or Withdrawn. Empty unless you are an agent on the request's desk.

get.summary: Get an intake request's status changes, newest first, in the tiers you can read.
get.description: Each change reports the status names as they were at the time. Without the request's substance, each change comes without its reason or who made it.

get.summary: Get the status workflow an intake request moves through.
get.description: Readable by anyone who can see the request, so its status history can be drawn on the workflow without workflow administration permissions.

post.summary: Give an employee access to an intake request as a participant.
post.description: An agent on the request's desk can always add someone; the requester and submitter can too, except on a private desk that does not allow it.

get.summary: Get a list of scoring models — the formula-driven models portfolios score and rank their projects with.
get.description: Each carries its UUID `id`, numeric `key`, name, description, state (Proposed, Active, Archived), and how many criteria, scales and outputs it has. Filter with `state`; only an Active model can be assigned to a portfolio, so pass `Active` to find the UUID that Portfolios_AssignScoringModel takes. A portfolio's current model is on Portfolios_GetPortfolio, and a project's on Projects_GetScoringContext.

get.summary: Get a scoring model with its criteria, rating scales and output formulas.
get.description: Criteria are what a project is rated on: one with a `scaleId` is rated by choosing a level of that scale, any other takes a number. Outputs are named formulas over the criteria's `token`s, and the one with `isPrimary` is the headline score; the formulas alone decide the score, so a criterion's `weight` is informational only. Accepts the model's UUID or numeric key.

isRelated.description:
Whether the entry was raised on another record and is listed here because its event names this one.
`aggregateType` and `aggregateId` are then that other record.

raisedOn.description:
The record a related entry was raised on. Null when the entry is not related, or when the record could
not be resolved, typically because it has since been removed.

missing — provided the User_ID parses as a valid email. Workaround for tenants whose ISU
ISSG doesn't grant Worker Data: Personal Contact Information.

When true, sync reads each worker's `Preferred_Name_Data` in preference to
`Legal_Name_Data`, falling back to legal per-component when a preferred component is
missing. Default off.

When true, names that come back from Workday in all-caps are title-cased before storage
(mixed-case input is preserved). Default true — most HRIS sources emit upper-cased legal
names that look inconsistent next to manually-entered records.

departmentOrganizationTypeId.description:
Workday `Organization_Type_ID` that drives `Employee.Department`. Defaults to
`SUPERVISORY` (Workday's universal reporting-hierarchy type). After the first init
probe, admins can pick from the discovered catalog (e.g. `COST_CENTER`,

Optional admin-configured rules that filter workers out of the sync. Each rule names an
Organization_Type_ID plus the WID of an org of that type; workers in that org are dropped
before upsert. Empty by default.

previousAverageDays.description: The same mean over the window immediately before this one.

cutAt.description:
The moment scope was frozen — the build or tag that cut it. Supplied rather than taken from the
clock, because cutting is often recorded after the fact. Required unless the deprecated
`CutDate` is sent instead.

cutDate.description: The day it was cut, read as 12:00 in the organization's default time zone.
cutDate.x-deprecatedMessage: Use CutAt. Removed in a future release.

workItemsCount.description:
Number of completed work items that contributed to this summary: items
with both an activated and a done timestamp, done after activated.

totalCycleTimeDays.description:
Sum of cycle times in days across the contributing items.
0 when `workItemsCount` is 0; treat that count, not this field,
as the sign that there is no data.

averageCycleTimeDays.description:
Mean cycle time in days, or null when there are no contributing items.
To combine summaries, sum `workItemsCount` and `totalCycleTimeDays`
rather than averaging this value.

CycleTimeSummary.description:
Cycle-time rollup over a set of completed work items.
Carries the underlying count and total so consumers can aggregate across
scopes without average-of-averages bias: sum `workItemsCount` and
`totalCycleTimeDays` across summaries, then divide the total by the count.

withdrawn.description: How many of that day's versions have since been withdrawn.

from.description:
When the measured window begins: the start of the iteration's first day in the team's time zone that day,
or in its zone on the last day when it has no operating model on the first.

until.description:
When the measured window ends, exclusive: the start of the day after the iteration's last, in
`timeZone`.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone the team's operating model has on the iteration's last day.

sizingMethod.description:
The estimate the team is measured in: its sizing method on the iteration's first day, or on its last when
its operating models begin inside the iteration.

completedWorkItems.description: Requirement-tier items that reached a Done-category status within the window, by done date. Removed work is left out.

inProgressWorkItems.description: Requirement-tier items in an In Progress-category status at `inProgressAsOf`.

inProgressAsOf.description:
When in progress was read: the window's end for a past iteration, now for the current one, and null for a
future one.

unestimatedWorkItems.description: Completed and in-progress items with no value in `sizingMethod`.

cycleTime.description: Cycle-time rollup of the completed items.

isHistoryIncomplete.description:
Whether in progress for a past iteration may be short, because a workspace holding the team's work has not
had its history read through to the end.

A Kanban team's metrics for the PI Iteration, measured by the iteration's dates in the team's time zone. Nothing
is scoped to an iteration for a Kanban team, so it has no total, committed or not-started figures.

(System.Text.Json per the Wolverine host configuration, so it renders as JSON).

DeadLetterEnvelopeQuery paging.

because users still sign in through it, with how many active identities remain bound.

The version deployed, when this deployment carries a single version. Its `name` is the
version number, which is what a reader identifies it by.

package.description:
The package deployed, when several components shipped as one unit. Exactly one of this and
`version` is set.

Whether it counts toward change failure rate. A failure before production is a failure that was
prevented, so only production counts.

What kind of target this is. Every delivery measure scoped to production counts on this rather
than on the name, which is free text and endlessly varied.

Position in a progressive rollout, lowest first. Environments sharing a ring are deployed to
together; the value carries no meaning beyond ordering.

deploymentCount.description: How many deployments have targeted it, so a caller can see what deactivating would affect.

windowDays.description: Days the window spans, so a caller can recompute the rate over any period.

combining windows should sum `count` and `windowDays` instead.

isMuted.description: Whether the caller has muted the record: they still follow it, but are told nothing about it.

FollowedRecordDto.description: A record the caller follows, as a list shows it.

FollowSort.description: The order the Following list is shown in.

isFollowing.description: Whether the caller follows the record.

followedOn.description: When the caller started following the record; null when they do not follow it.

FollowStatusDto.description: Whether the caller follows a record.

displayName.description: What to call this kind of record, such as "Project".

count.description: How many readable records of this type the caller follows.

FollowTypeCountDto.description: How many records of one owner type the caller follows.

count.description: How many readable followed records it holds.

FollowViewCountDto.description: How many followed records fall in one "needs a look" view.

shareOfTrialsSettingFinish.description:
The share of trials (0 to 1) in which waiting on the predecessor made the successor
finish later than its own backlog position allowed. Null when the successor cannot be
forecast.

reason.description: Why the forecast left the dependency out: Closes a Cycle or Predecessor Removed.

type.description: Why the work item could not be forecast: No Team, Not a Backlog Item or Not Enough History.

confidence.description: The share of trials, as a whole percent, that finished on or before `date`.

date.description: Null when that many trials did not finish within the forecast horizon.

ForecastTeamDto.description:
A team whose throughput a forecast drew on, and the history it was sampled from: whole UTC
days, inclusive.

FrozenStatusDto.description: The status a transition moved out of, as it was called at the time.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the system default, used by every team operating model that names no calendar.

operatingModelCount.description: How many team operating models name this calendar. A calendar in use cannot be deleted.

employeeCount.description: How many employees follow this calendar instead of the system default. A calendar in use cannot be deleted.

HolidayCalendarDetailsDto.description: A holiday calendar with its holidays.

holidayCount.description: How many holidays the calendar holds, across all years.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the system default, used by every team operating model that names no calendar.

HolidayCalendarListDto.description: A holiday calendar in a list.

HolidayDto.description: A day off in a holiday calendar.

date.description: The day off. A calendar holds at most one holiday per date.

name.description: What the day is, such as "New Year's Day".

IdentityMappingAction.description: What an admin decided about one external identity.

ImportDefinitionDto.description: One kind of import the caller may see.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

name.description: What your organization calls it — "Production", "prod-eu", "QA2".

ringOrder.description: Position in a progressive rollout, lowest first.

isActive.description:
Whether the environment is still deployed into. Blank means active; `false` creates it and
then retires it, for the environments a historical backfill's deployments still point at.

ImportDeploymentEnvironmentRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the deployment environment import.
An environment is identified by `Name`, which is unique across the organization. The
deployments import names its environment by this, so a file of environments is what a historical
backfill loads first.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

versionId.description: The version deployed, by id. Leave empty when a package was deployed.

packageId.description: The package deployed, by id. Leave empty when a version was deployed.

artifactId.description: The build that actually shipped — `4.8.2.008` where the version number is `4.8.2`.

startedAt.description: When the deployment began, with its offset.

outcome.description:
`Succeeded`, `Failed` or `RolledBack`, case-insensitively. Blank leaves the
deployment in flight.

completedAt.description:
When the deployment reached its outcome, with its offset. Required with an outcome. For a
rollback, when it succeeded.

rolledBackAt.description: When a rolled-back deployment was reverted, with its offset. Required for a rollback.

reason.description: Why it failed or was rolled back. Max 1024 chars.

ImportDeploymentRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the deployment import.
Exactly one of `VersionId` and `PackageId` is set, both by id. The
environment is named, because names are unique. A build number is never resolved to a version: the
row says which version it deployed and carries the build as its `ArtifactId`.
There is no status column. A row with no `Outcome` is still in flight; one with an
outcome is walked through the same transitions a person would record, with the real timestamps
supplied here. A rollback is recorded as a success first, so it needs both the time it completed
and the time it was reverted.
Timestamps are instants, and each must carry its offset (see `OffsetTimestamp`).

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it, and it is how a row is identified without depending on a display name.
Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the column itself must be
in the file.

employeeNumber.description: The employee's natural key, unique across the company.

hireDate.description: The date the employee was hired.

managerNumber.description: The manager's employee number. May name someone elsewhere in the file.

isActive.description: Whether the employee is currently active.

employeeType.description: The worker type (e.g. Employee, Contractor, Intern), mirroring the HRIS descriptor. Free-form.

additionalEmails.description:
Further work addresses for this person, semicolon-separated. `Email` stays the
primary; these are additional addresses the person is known by in other systems — typically ones
left behind by a domain or tenant move. Home and personal addresses do not belong here.

ImportEmployeeRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the employee import. References the row's manager by employee number so an entire
management tree can be imported at once; linkage is resolved server-side after all rows are created.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

planningIntervalId.description: The planning interval the objective belongs to, by id. Rows may name different intervals.

teamId.description: The team the objective belongs to, by id.

statusId.description: 1 Not Started, 2 In Progress, 3 Completed, 4 Canceled, 5 Missed.

startDate.description: Before TargetDate where both are given.

isStretch.description: Whether the objective is a stretch goal.

closedDateUtc.description: When the objective closed, in UTC. Required when the status is Completed or Canceled, and empty otherwise.

order.description: Display position within the team's objectives.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

start.description: The dates the interval ran over. Its iterations are generated inside this range.

end.description: The last date the interval ran over. On or after Start.

iterationWeeks.description:
The cadence the interval's iterations are generated from. There is no column for the iterations
themselves: an interval whose real history had irregular lengths or names is corrected afterwards
on its own dates screen.

iterationPrefix.description:
Prefixes each generated iteration's name, which is otherwise just its sequence number — so
iterations from different intervals stay tellable apart.

teamIds.description:
Semicolon-separated ids of the teams that ran the interval. Blank leaves the new interval with no
teams; nothing is ever replaced, since this import only creates.

ImportPlanningIntervalRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the planning interval import. The teams that ran the interval ride on the same
row as `TeamIds`, a semicolon-separated list of ids — the repo's multi-value column
convention — so one row is one planning interval and there is no second file.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

status.description: The portfolio's status.

createdOn.description:
The date the portfolio was proposed. Required on every row. Nothing stores it yet — a portfolio
keeps no creation date beyond the audit stamp, which records when the file was uploaded — but the
column is required now so that no file has to change on the day one is kept.

activatedOn.description:
The date the portfolio was activated. Required unless the portfolio is Proposed. There is no
closing date here: an import cannot close a portfolio, so the finalize import carries that one.

ImportPortfolioRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the portfolio import. `Status` is the status the portfolio should end
up in (case-insensitive), reached by replaying the real lifecycle transitions — which is why the
transition dates are on the row: a portfolio only ever gets its date range from those transitions,
never from creation.
Role columns hold semicolon-separated employee numbers, since a CSV cell cannot carry a list.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

type.description: Whether the row closes a program or a portfolio, which also says how Id is read.

id.description: The program or portfolio this row closes, per Type.

status.description: Programs: 'Completed' or 'Canceled'. Portfolios: 'Closed' or 'Archived'.

endDate.description: The portfolio's end date. Required for portfolio rows, ignored for program rows.

ImportPpmFinalizationRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the finalization import, closing one program or portfolio after its contents have
been imported. `Type` discriminates between the two (case-insensitive: "Program" /
"Portfolio") and says how to read `Id`.

unappliedRowCount.description: Rows neither applied nor rejected — what a resume would pick up.

isTerminal.description: Whether the run has finished, so a caller polling it knows when to stop.

ImportProcessDto.description: One import run, as the person who submitted it sees it.

ImportProcessPageDto.description: A page of runs, with the total so a UI can page without a second call.

ImportProcessRowPageDto.description: A page of row outcomes, with the total so a UI can page without a second call.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

productId.description: The product that has the dependency, by id.

dependsOnProductId.description: The product it relies on, by id.

strength.description:
`Hard` if the product stops working without it, `Soft` if it degrades but keeps working.
Required: there is no default, because a guessed strength misstates impact.

interactionStyles.description:
How the product reaches the one it relies on: `Synchronous`, `Asynchronous`, or both
separated by a semicolon or comma. Blank records none, which is not the same as recording that there
are none.

description.description: What the product relies on it for. Max 1024 chars.

startsOn.description: The day it began. Blank means today, so an `EndsOn` before today is refused.

endsOn.description: The last day it held. Blank means it still holds.

ImportProductDependencyRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the product dependency import: `ProductId` relies on
`DependsOnProductId`, both by id.
Record the most specific product known — the service, not the platform it belongs to. A product cannot
depend on itself or on anything above or below it in the tree, which is composition.
A dependency that stopped carries `EndsOn`. One whose strength changed is two rows on the
same pair: the first ending the day before the second starts.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it, and child rows name it as their ParentImportId. Leave a cell blank and the
row is known by its position instead — but a file with parents should fill it, since a position
is a fragile thing to reference. The column itself must be in the file.

productTypeName.description: The product type by name, which must already exist and be active.

parentImportId.description: The `ImportId` of another row in this file, or empty for a root product.

externalId.description: The product's identifier in the system that owns it.

status.description:
The status by name, which must belong to the product workflow. Defaults to the workflow's
initial status when the cell is blank.

tags.description:
The product's tags, as semicolon-separated `Category|Tag` pairs —
`Platform|ios;Platform|android;Compliance|pci-scope`.

ImportProductRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the product import.
`ParentImportId` must name another row in the same file by its `ImportId`,
or be empty for a root. A product already in the catalog cannot be named as a parent — this import
stands a catalog up rather than grafting single products onto one, which is what the screens are
for. Names cannot serve as the link: a tree legitimately holds the same name in two places, so
keying on names would make such a file unimportable.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

status.description: The program's status.

start.description: The timeline the program plans to run over.

end.description: On or after Start. Start and End are both empty or both set.

createdOn.description:
The date the program was proposed. Required on every row. Nothing stores it yet — a program keeps
no transition dates beyond the audit stamp, which records when the file was uploaded — but the
column is required now so that no file has to change on the day one is kept.

activatedOn.description:
The date the program became active. Required once the status is Active or Completed, optional on a
canceled program, and rejected on one that never got that far. There is no closing date here: an
import cannot complete or cancel a program, so the finalize import carries that one.

ImportProgramRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the program import. The owning portfolio is referenced by id and strategic themes
by a semicolon-separated list of ids; role columns hold semicolon-separated employee numbers.
`Status` is the status the program should end up in (case-insensitive), reached by replaying
the real lifecycle transitions.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

key.description: 2–20 uppercase letters and numbers, unique across projects. Tasks, stages and strategic initiatives name the project by it.

expenditureCategoryId.description: An expenditure category, by id. Create it in Settings first.

status.description: The project's status.

programId.description: The program this project belongs to, if any. The program must be in the same portfolio.

projectLifecycleId.description: The lifecycle to assign. Required for approved projects, and by any project with tasks.

start.description: The timeline the project plans to run over.

end.description: On or after Start. Start and End are both empty or both set.

createdOn.description:
The date the project was proposed. Required on every row, and what the project's opening status
history entry is dated — the audit stamp records when the file was uploaded, which is not the
same thing.

activatedOn.description:
The date the project became active. Required once the status is Active or Completed, optional on
a canceled project, and rejected on one that never got that far.

closedOn.description:
The date the project was completed or canceled — the status says which. Required on those two
statuses and rejected on the rest.

ImportProjectRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the project import. `Key` is the project's natural key, which project
tasks and strategic initiatives reference. The portfolio, program, expenditure category and lifecycle
are referenced by id; strategic themes and the role columns hold semicolon-separated lists.
`Status` is the status the project should end up in (case-insensitive), reached by replaying
the real lifecycle transitions.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

stageName.description: A stage of the project's assigned lifecycle, by name.

status.description: The stage status (case-insensitive): 'NotStarted', 'InProgress', 'Completed' or 'Canceled'.

ImportProjectStageRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the project stage import: sets one stage's status. The project is referenced by key
and the stage by name (stages come from the project's assigned lifecycle). The status is applied as given.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it, and child rows name it as their ParentImportId. Leave a cell blank and the
row is known by its position instead, but the column itself must be in the file.

projectKey.description: The project this task belongs to, by key.

stageName.description: A stage of the project's assigned lifecycle, by name.

parentImportId.description: The ImportId of the row this task nests under. Empty makes it a root task of its stage.

parentTaskId.description: The id of an existing task this one nests under. Cannot be combined with ParentImportId.

progress.description: Percent complete (0-100). Required for tasks, not allowed for milestones.

plannedStart.description: Planned start, for tasks. Milestones use PlannedDate instead.

plannedEnd.description: Planned end, for tasks. On or after PlannedStart.

plannedDate.description: The milestone's date. Only for milestones.

estimatedEffortHours.description: Estimated effort in hours. Greater than 0 when present.

assignees.description: Semicolon-separated employee numbers assigned to the task.

ImportProjectTaskRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the project task import. The project is referenced by key and the stage by name
(stages come from the project's assigned lifecycle). A task nests under another row in this file by its
`ParentImportId`, or under a task the project already has by `ParentTaskId`;
with neither it is a root task of its stage. Rows may be listed in any order — parents are applied
before children.

releaseImportId.description: The `ImportId` of the release row this row belongs to.

packageId.description: The package, by id. Required when `Kind` is `Package`.

versionId.description: The version, by id. Required when `Kind` is `Version`.

ImportReleaseContentRequest.description: A single CSV row for the contents file: one thing a release announces.

packageImportId.description: The `ImportId` of the package row this line belongs to.

versionNumber.description: The component's version in this package. Free text, never parsed.

kind.description: Whether the component changed in this package. `Changed` or `CarriedForward`.

ImportReleasePackageComponentRequest.description: A single CSV row for the manifest file: one component of one package.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it, and the manifest file names it to say which package a line belongs to.
Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the column itself must be
in the file.

version.description: The package's own version, distinct from any component's. Free text, never parsed.

targetDate.description: When the package is expected to ship.

releasedAt.description:
When the package shipped, with its offset — copy the completion time of the pipeline run that
shipped it as-is. Supplying it makes the package Released.

ImportReleasePackageRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the release package import — one package, without its manifest.
A package is identified by `Version` alone: it has no product, because it spans them.
Manifest lines arrive in a second file and point back here by this row's `ImportId`.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it, and the contents file names it to say which release a row belongs to. Leave
a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the column itself must be in the
file.

version.description: The release as the organization announces it — `2026.07`. Free text, never parsed.

productId.description: The product this release is announced under, if any, by id. Usually a product line.

targetDate.description: When the release is expected to be announced.

releasedDate.description:
When it was announced. Supplying it makes the release Released — and is refused while anything
it carries has not shipped.

sequence.description: A manual ordering override, for the rare case where chronology misleads.

notes.description: Product notes for this release, written for customers.

ImportReleaseRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the release import — one release, without its contents.
A release is identified by `Version` alone. `ProductId` is optional by
design: a release spanning product lines has no single owner, so requiring one would force a
misleading choice.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

teamId.description: The team the risk belongs to, by id.

reportedOnUtc.description: When the risk was reported, in UTC. Must be in the past.

reportedById.description: The employee who reported it, by id.

assigneeId.description: The employee the risk is assigned to, by id.

closedDateUtc.description: When the risk closed, in UTC. Required when StatusId is 2 (Closed), and empty otherwise. After ReportedOnUtc and in the past.

strategicInitiativeImportId.description:
The `ImportId` of the initiative row this KPI belongs to. Where that row left the column
blank its position stands in, so `1` reaches the first initiative — but a file carrying KPIs
should supply `ImportId`, since inserting a row silently re-parents every KPI below it.

prefix.description: A symbol shown before the value, such as "$".

suffix.description: A symbol shown after the value, such as "%".

targetDirection.description: Whether success means increasing or decreasing the value. Defaults to Increase.

ImportStrategicInitiativeKpiRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the strategic initiative KPI import, attached to its initiative by that row's
`ImportId`. KPIs are a separate file because an initiative has many of them, which a single
initiative row cannot carry.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it, and the KPI file names it to say which initiative a KPI belongs to. Leave a
cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the column itself must be in the
file.

status.description: The initiative's status.

end.description: The initiative's end date. On or after Start.

projectKeys.description: Semicolon-separated project keys the initiative delivers through.

ImportStrategicInitiativeRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the strategic initiative import. The owning portfolio is referenced by id and the
delivering projects by a semicolon-separated list of their keys; role columns hold semicolon-separated
employee numbers. `Status` is the status the initiative should end up in (case-insensitive),
reached by replaying the real lifecycle transitions.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

ImportStrategicThemeRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the strategic theme import. `State` is the theme's state on creation
(case-insensitive: "Proposed" / "Active" / "Archived"), applied directly rather than through the
activate/archive transitions.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

employeeNumber.description: The employee, by number. Must be an active employee.

roleName.description: A team member role, by name. The role must already exist.

ImportTeamMemberRequest.description:
A single CSV row for team staffing: places one employee on one team in one role, all by natural key.
Multiple roles for the same employee on the same team are expressed as multiple rows.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

childCode.description: The child team's code. May be a Team or a Team of Teams.

parentCode.description: The parent's code. Must be a Team of Teams, and cannot equal ChildCode.

start.description: When the membership begins. On or after both teams' active dates.

end.description: When the membership ends. On or after Start; blank for one still in place.

ImportTeamMembershipRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the team-hierarchy import: places a child team (or team of teams) under a parent
team of teams for a date range, all by natural key.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

code.description: The team's natural key: 2–10 uppercase letters and numbers, unique across teams.

activeDate.description: The date the team became active.

isActive.description: Whether the team is currently active.

inactiveDate.description: When the team was retired. Required when `IsActive` is `false`; must be after `ActiveDate`.

ImportTeamRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the unified team import. `Type` discriminates between a Team and a
Team of Teams (case-insensitive: "Team" / "TeamOfTeams"). Both share the same create shape.

importId.description:
The caller's own key for this row, unique within the file (case-insensitively). Results are
reported against it. Leave a cell blank and the row is known by its position instead, but the
column itself must be in the file.

productId.description: The product this version was cut against, by id. Must be a releasable type.

number.description: The version as the organization writes it. Free text, never parsed.

targetDate.description: When the version is expected to ship.

cutAt.description: When scope froze — the build or tag — with its offset. Supplying it makes the version Ready.

releasedAt.description: When it shipped, with its offset. Supplying it makes the version Released.

sequence.description: A manual ordering override, for the rare case where chronology misleads.

ImportVersionRequest.description:
A single CSV row for the version import.
The product is referenced by id, and a version is identified by that product together with its
`Number` — version strings are free text and only meaningful within one product, so two
products may each hold a `1.0.0`.
There is no status column: the moments decide where the version ends up. A row with neither is
planned, a `CutAt` makes it ready, and a `ReleasedAt` makes it
released. A released moment without a cut moment is legitimate — a version recorded after the fact
often has no record of when scope froze.
Both moments are instants and must carry their offset (see `OffsetTimestamp`): copy the
CI/CD timestamps as-is.

id.description: Connection Id.

externalId.description: External identifier for the work process.

id.description: Connection Id.

externalViewWorkItemUrlTemplate.description: A url template for external work items.  This template plus the work item external id will create a url to view the work item in the external system.

InstantWindowDto.description:
The moments from `earliest` to `latest`, both included. A null
`latest` means the window runs up to now, whenever the caller acts.

id.description: The channel's id, which a request refers to.

name.description: What the company calls the channel.

description.description: What belongs in the channel, when described.

order.description: Position in the list a requester chooses from, lowest first.

isActive.description: Whether new requests can be given this channel.

IntakeChannelDto.description: An intake channel: one of the places requests come from.

id.description: The channel's id.

name.description: What the company calls the channel.

IntakeChannelNavigationDto.description: A channel as a request refers to it.

id.description: The desk's id.

key.description: The desk's key.

name.description: What its members and administrators call the desk.

description.description: The requester-facing description of what kind of ask to bring here, which requesters choose by.

visibility.description: How much of a request on this desk reaches people outside it.

isRequesterSelectable.description: Whether a requester can pick this desk.

isOpen.description: Whether the desk accepts new requests.

requesterMayAddParticipants.description: On a private desk, whether the requester may add participants themselves.

offersAllChannels.description: Whether the desk offers every active company channel, including channels added later.

channelIds.description:
The company channels the desk chose, in the company's order, while it does not offer them all; an
archived one stays chosen but is not offered. Empty with bool IntakeDeskDto.OffersAllChannels false means the
desk offers none.

offersAllTagCategories.description: Whether the desk's agents tag along every active company tag axis, including axes added later.

tagCategoryIds.description:
The tag axes the desk chose, in the company's order, while it does not offer them all; an inactive one
stays chosen but is not offered. Empty with bool IntakeDeskDto.OffersAllTagCategories false means its agents tag
along none.

revision.description: How many changes the desk has recorded; sent back with a change so a stale one is refused.

members.description: The employees named on the desk, by name, with their roles.

waiting.description:
What is waiting on the desk, for its members and the Demand Management Admin; null for anyone else,
so a private desk's numbers never reach someone outside it.

canManage.description: Whether the reader may change the desk's details, settings and agents: a Desk Admin on it.

canAdminister.description: Whether the reader may change the desk's visibility and its Desk Admins: the Demand Management Admin.

canDelete.description: Whether the reader may delete the desk: the Demand Management Admin, and only while no request is on it.

IntakeDeskDto.description: An intake desk: what it takes, who works it, and how much of its requests the rest of the company reads.

to the default reaches it.

hasRequests.description: Whether any request is on the desk, which stops its workflow changing.

Whether the reader may choose the desk's workflow: a Desk Admin on it or the Demand Management Admin,
while no request is on it.

statuses.description:

statuses.description: The destination workflow's open statuses that need no reason, in the workflow's order.

shares its workflow, otherwise the one with the same meaning or name. Null when none fits, and the mover
must choose.

The statuses an intake request can arrive in when moved to a desk, and the one it arrives in unless the
mover chooses.

substance.description: The substance tier, or null when the reader may not see it.

canWithdraw.description: Whether the reader may withdraw the request: its requester, while it is open.

duplicateOf.description:

named or counted.

sourceSystem.description: The system the request was raised in.

participants.description: The people given access to the request beyond its requester and submitter.

origin.description: The upstream record the request arrived from, when it did not start in Wayd.

statusReason.description:

IntakeRequestSubstanceDto.description: The substance tier of an intake request: the ask itself and its own people.

key.description: The request's number, sequential across the install.

title.description: What is being asked for, in a line.

status.description: Where the request stands in its desk's review workflow, as the status was called when it moved there.

requester.description: The employee the request is for.

channel.description:

assignee.description: The member of the request's desk who owns it, when one is assigned.

needBy.description: When the request has to land and why, when it has a need-by date.

submittedOn.description: When the request was submitted, from which its age is read.

name.description: What the company calls the axis.

Whether a request can carry several tags from the axis. When false, tagging a request replaces the tag
it held on the axis. Fixed once the axis exists.

order.description: Position when presenting the axes, lowest first.

IntakeRequestTagCategoryDto.description: A tag axis reviewers file intake requests along, with its tags.

name.description: The label, unique within its axis.

would touch. Counts only visible requests, so it never discloses a private desk's.

IntakeRequestTagOptionDto.description: One tag on an axis, as the settings page and the pickers list it.

alias.description: The well-known meaning the status carries, as an intake request status alias value, or 0 for none.

description.description: What the status means, when the workflow's author said, written for anyone following a request.

recorded after the fact. Required unless the deprecated `ReleasedDate` is sent instead.

releasedAt.description:
The moment it shipped. This is what orders a version history, so it is supplied rather than
taken from the clock. Required unless the deprecated `ReleasedDate` is sent instead.

releasedDate.description: The day it shipped, read as 12:00 in the organization's default time zone.
releasedDate.x-deprecatedMessage: Use ReleasedAt. Removed in a future release.

userId.description:
The caller's user account id. Pass it only where a parameter's description says it takes a user
id; role, assignee and employeeId parameters take NavigationDto? MeResponse.Employee's id instead.

userName.description: The account's user name, usually the sign-in email.

employee.description:
The employee the account is linked to: its UUID `id` is what employeeId, role and assignee
parameters take for the caller. Null when the account has no linked employee, in which case
nothing in Wayd is recorded against the caller as a person.

roles.description: The names of the roles that grant the caller's permissions.

Who the caller is: their sign-in account and, more often what matters, the employee that account is
linked to. Wayd records people as employees, so roles, assignees, team memberships and allocations

Snapshot of the Wolverine durable message store: how many envelopes are currently persisted in
each lifecycle bucket. In a healthy system incoming/outgoing hover near zero — envelopes only
linger during backlog, scheduled delivery, or after an unclean shutdown.

batch is dropped at the top of the ranking.

beforeProjectId.description:
The anchor immediately below the batch in the ranking. Must already be ranked. Null when the
batch is dropped at the bottom of the ranking.

actorKind.description: How the newest change was made: a person directly, or the platform reacting for one.

reasons.description: Every reason the caller was told about this record, across the whole entry.

unreadCount.description: How many of the entry's notifications the caller has not read.

count.description: How many notifications the entry collapses.

isUnread.description: Whether anything in the entry is unread.

Progress points gained (or, negative, lost) since the last check. Null when
`progressAtLastCheck` is.

The objective's activity since the last check, newest first. With no check, the most recent
entries.

activityTruncated.description:
True when there is more activity in that period than is listed; page
PlanningIntervals_GetObjectiveActivities for the rest.

objective has no linked work.

Daily progress of the linked work from the interval's start to the earlier of today and the
interval's end.

Monte Carlo forecast of the linked work against `schedule.targetDate`.
